title.zh: 卷二百九十五 列傳第五十四 尹洙 孫甫 謝絳 葉清臣 楊察
title.en: Volume 295 Biographies 54: Yin Zhu, Sun Fu, Xie Jiang, Ye Qingchen, Yang Cha
title.raw: 卷二百九十五 列傳第五十四 尹洙 孫甫 謝絳 葉清臣 楊察 Volume 295 Biographies 54: Yin Zhu, Sun Fu, Xie Jiang, Ye Qingchen, Yang Cha

sentences.zh: 尹洙，字師魯，河南人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu, style name Shilu, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu, whose courtesy name was Shilu, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 少與兄源俱以儒學知名。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Yuan were both renowned for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth he and his older brother Yuan were both known for their learning in the Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調正平縣主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as registrar of Zhengping County.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he was appointed registrar of Zhengping County.

sentences.zh: 歷河南府戶曹參軍、安國軍節度推官、知光澤縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as registrar in the Henan prefectural office, as military adjutant under the Anyang Army commissioner, and as magistrate of Guangze County.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as a staff officer in the Henan prefecture, as a military adjutant on the Anyang circuit, and as prefect of Guangze.

sentences.zh: 舉書判拔萃，改山南東道節度掌書記、知伊陽縣，有能名。

translations.literal: Having passed the superior examination in legal memorials, he was transferred to secretary on the Shannan East circuit and magistrate of Yiyang County, and gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: When he placed at the top in the examination on legal judgments, he was moved to be secretary on the Shannan East circuit and prefect of Yiyang, where he won a name for administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 用大臣薦，召試，為館閣校勘，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: On recommendation of high ministers he was summoned for examination, appointed collator in the palace library, and promoted to Vice Director in the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by leading ministers, he was called to court for testing, made a collator in the Hanlin archives, and promoted to vice director in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 會范仲淹貶，敕榜朝堂，戒百官為朋黨。

translations.literal: It happened that Fan Zhongyan was demoted; an edict was posted in the court hall warning all officials against factional association.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Fan Zhongyan was demoted, and an imperial notice was displayed in the hall of audience forbidding officials to form factions.

sentences.zh: 洙上奏曰：「仲淹忠亮有素，臣與之義兼師友，則是仲淹之黨也。

translations.literal: Zhu submitted a memorial saying: "Zhongyan has long been known for his loyalty and integrity; between him and me our bond is both that of teacher and of friend — thus I am of Zhongyan's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu submitted a memorial: "Zhongyan's loyalty and uprightness are of long standing. My ties to him are those of both teacher and friend — so I too am one of Zhongyan's faction.

sentences.zh: 今仲淹以朋黨被罪，臣不可苟免。」

translations.literal: Now that Zhongyan is punished for factionalism, I cannot seek to escape unduly."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhongyan is condemned as a factionalist, I cannot seek to excuse myself."

sentences.zh: 宰相怒，落校勘，復為掌書記、監唐州酒稅。

translations.literal: The chief councilors were angry; he was removed from his collatorship and again made secretary and superintendent of the Tangzhou liquor tax.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were furious. He was stripped of his collatorship and sent back to serve as a circuit secretary and to supervise the liquor tax at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 西北久安，洙作《敘燕》、《息戍》二篇，以為武備不可弛。

translations.literal: When the northwest had long enjoyed peace, Zhu wrote two essays, "On Yan" and "Ending Frontier Garrison," holding that military readiness must not be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: With the northwest at peace for many years, Zhu composed two essays, Discourse on Yan and On Resting the Garrisons, arguing that military preparedness must not be allowed to lapse.

sentences.zh: 《敘燕》曰：

translations.literal: "On Yan" says:
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Yan reads:

sentences.zh: 「戰國世，燕最弱。

translations.literal: "In the Warring States era Yan was weakest.
translations.idiomatic: "In the Warring States period Yan was the weakest of the states.

sentences.zh: 二漢叛臣，持燕挾虜，蔑能自固，以公孫伯珪之強，卒制於袁氏。

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers of the two Han dynasties took Yan and held the barbarians hostage, yet could not hold firm; even with the strength of Gongsun Zan, in the end they were controlled by the Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times rebel ministers used Yan to shield themselves behind the northern tribes yet could not secure themselves; even with a commander as strong as Gongsun Zan, they were ultimately mastered by Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 獨慕容乘石虎亂，乃並趙。

translations.literal: Only the Murong clan, taking advantage of Shi Hu's disorder, then annexed Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Murong, seizing on the turmoil of Shi Hu's reign, was able to swallow Zhao.

sentences.zh: 雖勝敗異術，大概論其強弱，燕不能加趙。

translations.literal: Although victories and defeats differed in method, generally speaking of relative strength Yan could not surpass Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Though their methods of victory and defeat differed, on the whole Yan could not match Zhao in strength.

sentences.zh: 趙、魏一，則燕固不敵。

translations.literal: When Zhao and Wei were united, Yan naturally could not stand against them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao and Wei stood as one, Yan could not hope to prevail.

sentences.zh: 唐三盜連衡百餘年，虜未嘗越燕侵趙、魏，是燕獨能支虜也。

translations.literal: Through the Tang, the Three Brigands united in alliance for more than a hundred years, and the barbarians never crossed Yan to invade Zhao and Wei — thus Yan alone could sustain the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: For over a century under the Tang the Three Brigands kept their alliance, and the northern tribes never crossed Yan to strike at Zhao and Wei — Yan alone could hold them at bay.

sentences.zh: 自燕入於契丹，勢日熾大。

translations.literal: Once Yan passed into Khitan hands, their power grew daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan fell to the Khitan, their power grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 顯德世，雖復三關，尚未盡燕南地。

translations.literal: In the Xiande reign they recovered the three passes but had not yet taken all the land south of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era the three passes were recovered, yet the lands south of Yan were not fully regained.

sentences.zh: 國初，始與並合，勢益張，然止命偏師備禦。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty they began to be fully annexed, and their power grew still greater; yet they only ordered detached forces to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding the two realms were finally united, and Khitan strength swelled further — yet the court only stationed detached forces to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蜀伐吳，泰然不以兩河為顧，是趙、魏足以制之明矣。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Shu and Wu, it remained calm and did not turn attention to the two He river regions — thus Zhao and Wei were clearly sufficient to control them.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies marched against Shu and Wu, the court remained untroubled about the two He regions — a clear sign that Zhao and Wei were enough to keep the Khitan in check.

sentences.zh: 幷寇既平，悉天下銳專力契丹，不能攘尺寸地。

translations.literal: Once the united enemy had been pacified, the empire marshaled all its elite strength against the Khitan yet could not recover a span of territory.
translations.idiomatic: After the northern enemy was subdued, the empire poured every elite force against the Khitan yet could not win back so much as a foot of ground.

sentences.zh: 頃嘗以百萬眾駐趙、魏，訖敵退莫敢抗，世多咎其不戰。

translations.literal: Not long ago a force of a million encamped in Zhao and Wei; when the enemy withdrew none dared resist, and many of the age criticized them for not fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a host of a million was stationed in Zhao and Wei; when the enemy withdrew no one dared give battle, and many blamed the commanders for failing to fight.

sentences.zh: 然我眾負城，有內顧心，戰不必勝，不勝則事亟矣，故不戰未嘗咎也。

translations.literal: Yet our multitude relied on fortified cities and had thoughts of turning homeward; if they fought victory was not assured, and without victory matters would be urgent — hence not fighting was never blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our troops leaned on walled cities and longed for home; battle offered no certainty of victory, and defeat would have made the crisis immediate — so refraining from battle was never truly faulted.

sentences.zh: 原其弊，在兵不分。

translations.literal: Examining the root of the trouble, it lay in not dividing the army.
translations.idiomatic: The root of the defect lay in failing to divide the army.

sentences.zh: 設兵為三，壁於爭地，掎角以疑其勢，設覆以待其進。

translations.literal: Suppose the army were divided into three, fortified at contested ground, pincering to confuse their momentum, and ambushes laid to await their advance.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the forces into three, fortify contested ground, strike from two sides to unsettle the enemy, and lay ambushes to meet their advance.

sentences.zh: 邊壘素固，驅民以守之，俾其兵頓堅城之下，乘間夾擊，無不勝矣。

translations.literal: Border ramparts being long solid, drive the people to defend them, so that the enemy's troops stall under strong walls, and strike from multiple directions at an opportune moment — there would be no defeat.
translations.idiomatic: With border fortifications already strong, mobilize the people to hold them, pin the enemy beneath those walls, and strike from both flanks at the right moment — victory would be assured.

sentences.zh: 蓋兵不分有六弊：使敵蓄勇以待戰，無他枝梧，一也；

translations.literal: For not dividing the army there are six harms: letting the enemy store up courage to await battle with no other threat, first;
translations.idiomatic: Not dividing the army brings six harms: the enemy can gather its strength for a single battle with no distraction elsewhere — the first harm;

sentences.zh: 我眾則士怠，二也；

translations.literal: When our forces are numerous the soldiers grow slack, second;
translations.idiomatic: when our numbers are great the troops grow lax — the second;

sentences.zh: 前世善將兵者必問幾何，今以中才盡主之，三也；

translations.literal: In former ages skilled commanders always asked how many troops they would have; now men of middling talent are put in charge of all, third;
translations.idiomatic: skilled generals of old always asked how many men they would command, yet today men of only middling ability are placed over the whole host — the third;

sentences.zh: 大眾儻北，彼遂長驅無復顧忌，四也；

translations.literal: If the great host should move north, the enemy would then drive deep without further restraint, fourth;
translations.idiomatic: if the main army marches north, the enemy can ride deep without further restraint — the fourth;

sentences.zh: 重兵一屬，根本虛弱，纖人易以幹說，五也；

translations.literal: With heavy forces under a single command the root is weakened and petty men easily gain influence, fifth;
translations.idiomatic: when all heavy forces answer to one man the heartland is left weak and petty men can easily sway policy — the fifth;

sentences.zh: 雖委大柄，不無疑貳，復命貴臣監督，進退皆由中御，失於應變，六也。

translations.literal: Even when great authority is entrusted, doubt is not absent; high ministers are again appointed to supervise, and advance and retreat are all decided from the center — losing flexibility in response, sixth.
translations.idiomatic: even when full authority is granted, suspicion remains; eminent ministers are sent to oversee, and every move must be approved from the capital — losing the power to adapt — the sixth.

sentences.zh: 兵分則盡易其弊，是有六利也。

translations.literal: If the army is divided all these harms are easily reversed — thus there are six benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the army and all six harms are readily reversed — that is the sixfold gain.

sentences.zh: 勝敗兵家常勢。

translations.literal: Victory and defeat are the constant pattern of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat are the common lot of armies.

sentences.zh: 悉內以擊外，失則舉所有以棄之，苻堅淝水、哥舒翰潼關是也。

translations.literal: To gather all within to strike outward — if one fails, everything is thrown away: Fu Jian at the Fei River and Geshu Han at Tong Pass are examples.
translations.idiomatic: Mass every resource at home to strike abroad, and one defeat costs everything — as with Fu Jian at the Fei River and Geshu Han at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 是則制敵在謀不在眾。

translations.literal: Thus controlling the enemy lies in strategy, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Controlling the enemy depends on design, not on numbers.

sentences.zh: 以趙、魏、燕南，益以山西，民足以守，兵足以戰。

translations.literal: With Zhao, Wei, and southern Yan, augmented by Shanxi, the people are sufficient to defend and the troops sufficient to fight.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhao, Wei, southern Yan, and Shanxi besides, the population is enough to hold the line and the soldiers enough to fight.

sentences.zh: 分而帥之，將得專制，就使偏師挫衄，他眾尚奮，詎能繫國安危哉？

translations.literal: Divide and command them; generals gain full discretion — even if a detached force suffers setback, other bodies still fight on; how could the fate of the state hang on it?
translations.idiomatic: Divide the forces and let each commander act on his own; even if one wing is beaten, the others remain eager — how could the nation's fate hang on a single clash?

sentences.zh: 故師覆於外而本根不搖者，善敗也。

translations.literal: Thus when armies are destroyed abroad yet the root is unshaken, that is skill in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When armies are broken in the field yet the foundation does not tremble, that is mastery even in defeat.

sentences.zh: 昔者六國各有地千里，師敗於秦，散而復振，幾百戰猶未及其都，守國之固也。

translations.literal: Formerly the six states each had a thousand li of territory; armies defeated by Qin scattered and rallied again — after hundreds of battles Qin still had not reached their capitals: such was the solidity of defending a state.
translations.idiomatic: In old times the six states each held a thousand li; beaten by Qin they scattered and regrouped, and after hundreds of battles Qin had still not reached their capitals — that is what it means to defend a realm securely.

sentences.zh: 陳勝、項梁舉關東之眾，朝敗而夕滅，新造之勢也。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang raised the hosts east of the Pass; defeated in the morning, extinguished by evening — such was a newly forged power.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang raised the armies east of the Pass; defeated at dawn, they were gone by dusk — the fate of a power newly forged.

sentences.zh: 以天下之廣謀其國，不若千里之固，而襲新造之勢，僥幸於一戰，庸非惑哉？

translations.literal: To plan one's state with the breadth of all under Heaven is not like the solidity of a thousand li; yet to imitate a newly forged power and gamble on a single battle — is this not delusion?
translations.idiomatic: To stake the wide realm on one plan is not like securing a thousand li; yet to imitate a fledgling uprising and stake everything on one battle — is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 兵既久弭，士大夫誦習，謂百世不復用，非甚妄者不談。

translations.literal: With arms long stilled, scholar-officials recite and study, saying they will not be used for a hundred generations; none but the most reckless speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: With war long stilled, the literati recite their texts and declare that arms will not be needed for a hundred generations; only the most reckless still speak of war.

sentences.zh: 然兵果廢則已，儻後世復用之，鑒此少以悟世主，故跡其勝敗云。」

translations.literal: Yet if arms are truly abandoned, so be it; should later ages use them again, let this serve as a mirror to awaken rulers — hence I trace their victories and defeats."
translations.idiomatic: If arms are truly to be cast aside, so be it; but should later ages take them up again, let this brief record awaken their rulers — hence I have traced these victories and defeats."

sentences.zh: 《息戍》曰：

translations.literal: "Ending Frontier Garrison" says:
translations.idiomatic: On Resting the Garrisons reads:

sentences.zh: 「國家割棄朔方，西師不出三十年，而亭徼千里，環重兵以戍之。

translations.literal: "The state abandoned Shuofang; western armies did not march out for thirty years, yet watchtowers and beacons stretch a thousand li, ringed by heavy forces to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: "The state surrendered Shuofang, and for thirty years no western expedition was launched — yet beacon towers line a thousand li of frontier, ringed by heavy garrisons.

sentences.zh: 雖種落屢擾，即時輯定，然屯戍之費，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: Although tribal groups often raided and were promptly pacified, the cost of garrison duty was already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Though the tribes raided again and again and were quickly subdued, the cost of maintaining those garrisons had already grown enormous.

sentences.zh: 西戎為寇，遠自周世，西漢先零，東漢燒當，晉氐、羌，唐禿髪，歷朝侵軼，為國劇患。

translations.literal: Western Rong raids extend back to the Zhou: Western Han Xianlian, Eastern Han Shaodang, Jin Di and Qiang, Tang Tufa — dynasty after dynasty they raided and were a grave national affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Western raids date back to the Zhou — the Xianlian in Western Han, the Shaodang in Eastern Han, the Di and Qiang in Jin, the Tufa in Tang — generation after generation they harried the borders and were a grave national scourge.

sentences.zh: 興師定律，皆有成功，而勞弊中國，東漢尤甚，費用常以億計。

translations.literal: Raising armies and setting laws all met with success, yet they exhausted China; Eastern Han suffered especially, costs often reckoned in hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty that raised armies and set policy achieved success, yet each wore down the heartland — Eastern Han most of all, with costs often running into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 孝安世，羌叛十四年，用二百四十億。

translations.literal: In the An reign of Emperor Xiao, the Qiang rebelled for fourteen years, costing 24 billion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An the Qiang rebelled for fourteen years, consuming 24 billion in expenditure.

sentences.zh: 永和末，復經七年，用八十餘億。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yonghe reign another seven years passed, costing more than 8 billion.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yonghe era another seven years of war cost more than 8 billion.

sentences.zh: 及段紀明，用裁五十四億，而剪滅殆盡。

translations.literal: Under Duan Jiming the cost was only 5.4 billion, and the rebels were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Under Duan Jiming the cost was only 5.4 billion, and the rebels were all but wiped out.

sentences.zh: 今西北涇原、邠寧、秦鳳、鄜延四帥，戍卒十餘萬。

translations.literal: Today the four frontier commands of Jingyuan, Binning, Qinfeng, and Fuyan have more than a hundred thousand garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Today the four northwestern commands — Jingyuan, Binning, Qinfeng, and Fuyan — keep more than a hundred thousand men on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一卒歲給，無慮二萬，騎卒與冗卒，較其中者，總廩給之數，恩賞不在焉，以十萬較之，歲用二十億。

translations.literal: Annual provision for one soldier is no less than twenty thousand; comparing cavalry and supernumerary troops at the midpoint, the total grain allowance — favors and rewards aside — for a hundred thousand men comes to two billion a year.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier costs at least twenty thousand a year in supplies; counting cavalry and auxiliaries at a middle estimate, grain payments alone for a hundred thousand men run to two billion yearly, not counting rewards.

sentences.zh: 自靈武罷兵，計費六百餘億，方前世數倍矣。

translations.literal: Since troops were withdrawn from Lingzhou the total cost has exceeded 60 billion — several times that of earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Since the withdrawal from Lingzhou the total has passed 60 billion — several times what earlier dynasties spent.

sentences.zh: 平世屯戍，且猶若是，後雖有他警，不可一日輟去，是十萬眾，有增而無損期也。

translations.literal: In peaceful times garrison costs are already so; though other alarms may come later, they cannot be dismissed for a day — these hundred thousand men can only grow, never shrink, for the foreseeable future.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peacetime garrison costs run this high; though new alarms may arise, the garrisons cannot stand down for a day — this host of a hundred thousand can only grow, never shrink, for years to come.

sentences.zh: 國家厚利募商入粟，傾四方之貨，然無水漕之運，所輓致亦不過被邊數郡爾。

translations.literal: The state offers rich profits to recruit merchants to bring grain, drawing goods from all quarters — yet without water transport the haul reaches only a few border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court pays lavish profits to lure merchants to haul grain, draining goods from every region — yet without canal transport the supply reaches only a handful of border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歲不常登，廩有常給，頃年亦嘗稍匱矣。

translations.literal: Harvests are not always abundant, yet the granaries must be constantly supplied; in recent years stores have even run somewhat short.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests are not always good, yet the granaries must be fed without pause; in recent years reserves have even grown thin.

sentences.zh: 儻其乘我薦饑，我必濟師，饋饟當出於關中，則未戰而西垂已困，可不慮哉？

translations.literal: If they strike when we suffer famine and we must reinforce, provisions must come from Guanzhong — then before battle the western frontier is already exhausted; should this not be considered?
translations.idiomatic: If the tribes strike when famine grips us and we must send reinforcements, supplies must come from Guanzhong — the western frontier would be exhausted before a battle was fought. Should we not reckon with that?

sentences.zh: 按唐府兵，上府千二百人，中府千人，下府八百人。

translations.literal: According to Tang frontier militia: upper prefectures 1,200 men, middle 1,000, lower 800.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang frontier-militia system, upper prefectures fielded 1,200 men, middle ones 1,000, and lower ones 800.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若籍丁民為兵，擬唐置府，頗損其數。

translations.literal: For the present plan, nothing is better than registering adult males as soldiers, following the Tang prefectural militia with somewhat reduced numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The best policy today is to register adult males as soldiers, reviving the Tang militia prefectures on a somewhat reduced scale.

sentences.zh: 又今邊鄙雖有鄉兵之制，然止極塞數郡，民籍寡少，不足備敵。

translations.literal: Though the frontier today has a militia system, it extends only to the outermost border prefectures; registered households are few and insufficient to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier does have a militia system, but it covers only the outermost border counties; registered households are too few to face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 料京兆西北數郡，上戶可十餘萬，中家半之，當得兵六七萬。

translations.literal: Estimating several prefectures northwest of Jingzhao, wealthy households may number more than a hundred thousand; middle households half that — one could raise sixty or seventy thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Counting several prefectures northwest of the capital, wealthy households may exceed a hundred thousand; middle households half as many — yielding sixty or seventy thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 質其賦無他易，賦以帛名者不易以五穀，畜馬者又蠲其雜徭。

translations.literal: Pledge their tax payments without other exchange; taxes reckoned in silk are not exchanged for grain, and those who keep horses are also exempted from miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Let them pledge their tax payments in kind without other levies; taxes assessed in silk need not be converted to grain, and horse-keepers should be freed from miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 民幸於庇宗，樂然隸籍。

translations.literal: The people, glad of the protection of their clans, would gladly enroll.
translations.idiomatic: Glad of clan protection, the people would enroll willingly.

sentences.zh: 農隙講事，登材武者為什長、隊正，盛秋旬閱，常若寇至。

translations.literal: In the farming slack season drill them; appoint the able in arms as squad and company leaders; in the height of autumn review them every ten days as though the enemy were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Drill them in the farming slack season; promote the martially gifted as squad and company leaders; in late autumn hold ten-day reviews as if the enemy were upon them.

sentences.zh: 以關內、河東勁兵傅之，盡罷京師禁旅，慎簡守帥，分其統，專其任。

translations.literal: Attach the strong troops of Guannei and Hedong to them, disband the capital guard entirely, choose frontier commanders carefully, divide their command, and give each full responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Attach the crack troops of Guannei and Hedong, disband the capital guard, choose frontier commanders with care, divide command among them, and give each full responsibility.

sentences.zh: 分統則兵不重，專任則將益勵，堅其守備，習其形勢，積粟多，教士銳，使虜眾無隙可窺，不戰而懾。

translations.literal: Divided command keeps forces from over-concentrating; sole responsibility makes generals strive harder; strengthen defenses, learn the terrain, store grain abundantly, train soldiers keenly — let the barbarian hosts find no opening, and they will be awed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Split command so no single army grows too heavy; sole responsibility makes generals strive; fortify defenses, master the terrain, stock grain, sharpen troops — leave the barbarians no gap to probe, and they will be cowed without a battle.

sentences.zh: 《兵志》所謂「無恃其不來，恃吾有以待之」，其廟勝之策乎？」

translations.literal: As the Military Treatise says, "Do not rely on the enemy not coming; rely on being ready to meet him" — is this not the strategy of victory decided in the temple?"
translations.idiomatic: As the Art of War says, "Do not count on the enemy not coming; count on being ready when he does" — is that not victory won before the campaign begins?"

sentences.zh: 又為《述享》、《審斷》、《原刑》、《敦學》、《矯察》、《考績》、《廣諫》，凡《雜議》共九篇上之。

translations.literal: He also wrote "On Sacrificial Enjoyment," "On Judgment," "On the Origin of Punishment," "On Encouraging Learning," "On Rectifying Investigation," "On Assessing Performance," and "On Broad Remonstrance" — nine essays in all under the title "Miscellaneous Discourses," which he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote On Sacrificial Rites, On Judgment, On the Origins of Punishment, On Encouraging Learning, On Rectifying Investigation, On Assessing Performance, and On Broad Remonstrance — nine essays in all under the title Miscellaneous Discourses, which he submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，大將葛懷敏辟為經略判官。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, the great general Ge Huaimin recruited him as frontier commissioner's adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, the commander Ge Huaimin recruited him as adjutant on the frontier commission.

sentences.zh: 洙雖用懷敏辟，尤為韓琦所深知。

translations.literal: Though Zhu entered service through Huaimin's recruitment, he was especially well understood by Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhu had entered through Ge Huaimin's commission, Han Qi knew his worth especially well.

sentences.zh: 頃之，劉平、石元孫戰敗，朝廷以夏竦為經略、安撫使，范仲淹、韓琦副之，復以洙為判官。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated in battle; the court appointed Xia Song frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner, with Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi as deputies, and again made Zhu adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated; the court named Xia Song frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner, with Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi as deputies, and again appointed Zhu adjutant.

sentences.zh: 洙數上疏論兵，請便殿召對二府大臣議邊事，及講求開寶以前用兵故實，特出睿斷，以重邊計。

translations.literal: Zhu repeatedly submitted memorials on military affairs, asking that the Two Departments be summoned to the side hall to discuss border affairs, and that precedents for warfare before the Kaibao era be studied — urging a special imperial decision to give weight to frontier planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu repeatedly memorialized on military affairs, asking that ministers of the Two Departments be called to the side hall to discuss the border, and that precedents for warfare before the Kaibao era be studied — urging the emperor to decide personally and give real weight to frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 又請減並柵壘，召募土兵，省騎軍，增步卒。

translations.literal: He also asked to reduce and merge stockades, recruit local militia, cut cavalry, and increase infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged reducing and merging stockades, recruiting local militia, trimming cavalry, and adding infantry.

sentences.zh: 又上鬻爵令。

translations.literal: He also submitted a proposal on selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a proposal on the sale of official ranks.

sentences.zh: 時詔問攻守之計，竦具二策，令琦與洙詣闕奏之。

translations.literal: At that time an edict asked for plans of attack and defense; Xia Song set forth two strategies and ordered Han Qi and Zhu to come to court and present them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court asked for plans of attack and defense, Xia Song drafted two strategies and sent Han Qi and Zhu to present them at court.

sentences.zh: 帝取攻策，以洙為集賢校理。

translations.literal: The emperor chose the attack strategy and made Zhu collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose the offensive plan and appointed Zhu collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 洙遂趨延州謀出兵，而仲淹持不可。

translations.literal: Zhu then hurried to Yanzhou to plan an expedition, but Fan Zhongyan held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu hurried to Yanzhou to plan a campaign, but Fan Zhongyan insisted it should not go forward.

sentences.zh: 還至慶州，會任福敗於好水川，因發慶州部將劉政銳卒數千，趨鎮戎軍赴救，未至，賊引去。

translations.literal: Returning to Qingzhou, it happened that Ren Fu was defeated at Hao River; Zhu therefore sent several thousand elite troops under the Qingzhou officer Liu Zheng toward Zhenrong Army to rescue them; before they arrived the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Qingzhou, Ren Fu was defeated at Hao River; Zhu sent several thousand elite troops under the Qingzhou officer Liu Zheng toward Zhenrong to rescue them, but the enemy withdrew before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 夏竦奏洙擅發兵，降通判濠州。

translations.literal: Xia Song memorialized that Zhu had dispatched troops on his own authority and demoted him to vice prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song reported that Zhu had mobilized troops without authorization and demoted him to vice prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 當時言者謂福之敗，由參軍耿傅督戰太急。

translations.literal: Commentators at the time said Fu's defeat came because the adjutant Geng Fu pressed the battle too hard.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said Ren Fu's defeat came because the adjutant Geng Fu had pressed the battle too hard.

sentences.zh: 後得傅書，乃戒福使持重，毋輕進。

translations.literal: Later Fu's letter was obtained; it had warned Fu to be cautious and not advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Geng Fu's letter was found; it had warned Ren Fu to be cautious and not advance rashly.

sentences.zh: 洙以傅文吏，無軍責而死於行陣，又為時所誣，遂作《憫忠》、《辨誣》二篇。

translations.literal: Zhu held that Fu, a civil official with no military duty, had died in battle and had also been slandered by the age; he therefore wrote "Lament for the Loyal" and "Refuting Slander."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu held that Geng Fu, a civil official with no military command, had died in battle and been slandered by his contemporaries; he wrote Lament for the Loyal and Refuting Slander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，韓琦知秦州，辟洙通判州事，加直集賢院。

translations.literal: Before long Han Qi became prefect of Qinzhou, recruited Zhu as vice prefect, and added him as direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Han Qi became prefect of Qinzhou, recruited Zhu as vice prefect, and gave him the additional title of academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 上奏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「漢文帝盛德之主，賈誼論當時事勢，猶云可為慟哭。

translations.literal: "Emperor Wen of Han was a ruler of great virtue; when Jia Yi discussed the situation of the time, he still said one could weep for it.
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wen of Han was a ruler of surpassing virtue; when Jia Yi surveyed the affairs of his day, he still said the situation could move one to tears.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝外制四夷，以強主威，徐樂、嚴安尚以陳勝亡秦、六卿篡晉為戒。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu outwardly subdued the four barbarians to strengthen imperial authority; yet Xu Yue and Yan An still took Chen Sheng's overthrow of Qin and the six ministers' usurpation of Jin as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu subdued the four quarters to magnify imperial might; yet Xu Yue and Yan An still warned of Chen Sheng's overthrow of Qin and the six ministers' seizure of Jin.

sentences.zh: 二帝不以危亂滅亡為諱，故子孫保有天下者十餘世。

translations.literal: These two emperors did not shrink from speaking of peril and ruin; hence their descendants held the realm for more than ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: Those two emperors did not shrink from naming danger and ruin; that is why their line held the realm for more than ten generations.

sentences.zh: 秦二世時，關東盜起。

translations.literal: In the time of the Second Emperor of Qin, bandits rose east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Second Emperor of Qin, rebels rose east of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 或以反者聞，二世怒，下吏；

translations.literal: When word of rebels was reported, the Second Emperor was angry and punished the officials;
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported rebels, the Second Emperor flew into a rage and punished the messenger;

sentences.zh: 或曰逐捕今盡，不足憂，乃悅。

translations.literal: when another said the pursuit would soon capture them all and there was nothing to worry about, he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: when another said the pursuit would soon capture them all and there was nothing to fear, he was pleased.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，四方兵起，左右近臣皆隱賊數，不以實聞，或言賊多者，輒被詰。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yang of Sui, armies rose on all sides; close attendants all concealed the number of rebels and did not report truthfully; whoever said the rebels were numerous was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang of Sui, armies rose on every side; close attendants hid the rebel numbers and would not report truthfully; whoever said the rebels were many was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 二帝以危亂滅亡為諱，故秦、隋宗社數年為丘墟。

translations.literal: These two emperors shrank from naming peril and ruin; hence the altars of Qin and Sui were rubble within a few years.
translations.idiomatic: Those two emperors would not hear of peril and ruin; within a few years the houses of Qin and Sui were heaps of rubble.

sentences.zh: 陛下視今日天下之治，孰與漢文？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, compare the governance of the realm today — which is it closer to, Han Wen?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, compare the governance of the realm today — is it closer to that of Han Wen?

sentences.zh: 威制四夷，孰與漢武？

translations.literal: In awe-inspiring control of the four barbarians — which is it closer to, Han Wu?
translations.idiomatic: In awe-inspiring control of the four quarters — is it closer to that of Han Wu?

sentences.zh: 國家基本仁德，陛下慈孝愛民，誠萬萬於秦、隋矣。

translations.literal: The state's foundation is benevolence and virtue; Your Majesty is filial, benevolent, and loves the people — truly ten thousand times above Qin and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The state's foundation is benevolence and virtue; Your Majesty is filial, benevolent, and loves the people — truly incomparably above Qin and Sui.

sentences.zh: 至於西有不臣之虜，北有強大之鄰，非特閭巷盜賊之勢也。

translations.literal: Yet in the west there is an unsubmissive barbarian, and in the north a powerful neighbor — this is not merely the menace of alleyway bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the west stands an unsubmissive barbarian power, and in the north a mighty neighbor — this is no mere threat of street robbers.

sentences.zh: 自西夏叛命四年，幷塞苦數擾，內地疲遠輸。

translations.literal: Since Western Xia rebelled four years ago, the Bing frontier has suffered repeated disturbances, and the interior has been exhausted by distant transport.
translations.idiomatic: Four years since Western Xia rebelled, the Bing frontier has been harried again and again, and the heartland is worn down supplying distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 兵久於外而休息無期，卒有乘弊而起。

translations.literal: Troops have long been abroad while rest has no fixed term; soldiers may rise up exploiting weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The army has been in the field for years with no end to rest in sight; the rank and file may seize a moment of weakness to rise up.

sentences.zh: 《兵法》所謂「雖有智者，不能善其後」。

translations.literal: What the Art of War calls, "Even with a wise man, one cannot make good what comes after."
translations.idiomatic: As the Art of War says: "Even the wise cannot set right what follows."

sentences.zh: 當此之時，陛下宜夙夜憂懼，所以慮事變而塞禍源也。

translations.literal: At such a time Your Majesty ought to worry day and night—this is how to consider change and block the sources of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In such a moment Your Majesty should worry day and night—that is how to foresee change and choke off the springs of disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下延訪邊事，容納直言，前世人主。

translations.literal: Your Majesty extends inquiry into border affairs and accepts blunt speech—sovereigns of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks counsel on frontier affairs and accepts blunt speech—sovereigns of former ages

sentences.zh: 勤勞寬大，未有能遠過者。

translations.literal: in diligence and generosity—none could far surpass.
translations.idiomatic: in diligence and magnanimity—none could come close.

sentences.zh: 然未聞以宗廟為憂，危亡為懼，此賤臣所以感憤於邑而不已也。

translations.literal: Yet I have not heard that you take the ancestral temple as your worry or peril of ruin as your fear; this is why this low official is stirred in my breast and cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have not heard you treat the ancestral altars as your concern or the threat of ruin as your fear—and that is why this humble official is stirred in my breast and cannot hold my peace.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 今命令數更，恩寵過濫，賜與不節。

translations.literal: Now orders change frequently, favor is lavished excessively, and grants are without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Today commands shift constantly, favor is poured out without measure, and gifts know no limit.

sentences.zh: 此三者，戒之慎之，在陛下所行爾，非有難動之勢也。

translations.literal: These three—warn and be careful of them; they lie in what Your Majesty does—there is no situation hard to move.
translations.idiomatic: These three demand vigilance; they rest entirely in what Your Majesty does—there is no force beyond your reach.

sentences.zh: 而因循不革，弊壞日甚。

translations.literal: Yet you cling to the old ways without reform, and the ills worsen daily.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cling to old habits without reform, and the damage grows worse each day.

sentences.zh: 臣謂陛下不以宗廟為憂、危亡為懼者，以此。

translations.literal: Your subject says that Your Majesty does not take the ancestral temple as worry or peril of ruin as fear—for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant says that Your Majesty does not treat the ancestral altars as your concern or the threat of ruin as your fear—and that, I believe, is why.

sentences.zh: 未命令者，人主所以取信於下也。

translations.literal: As for orders—they are how the sovereign wins trust from below.
translations.idiomatic: As for commands—they are how a ruler wins the trust of those below.

sentences.zh: 異時民間，朝廷降一命令，皆竦視之；

translations.literal: In former times among the people, when the court issued a single order, all stood in awe to receive it;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when the court issued an order, the people received it with awe;

sentences.zh: 今則不然，相與竊語，以為不久當更，既而信然，此命令日輕於下也。

translations.literal: now it is not so: they whisper among themselves that it will soon change—and so it proves; thus orders daily grow light below.
translations.idiomatic: now it is otherwise: they whisper that it will soon change—and they are right; commands grow lighter in the eyes of the people day by day.

sentences.zh: 命令輕，則朝廷不尊矣。

translations.literal: When orders are light, the court is not honored.
translations.idiomatic: When commands carry little weight, the court is not honored.

sentences.zh: 又聞群臣有獻忠謀者，陛下始甚聽之，年復一人沮之，則意移矣。

translations.literal: I also hear that when ministers offer loyal plans Your Majesty at first listens closely, but after a year someone obstructs them and your intent shifts.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that when ministers offer loyal counsel Your Majesty at first listens closely, yet before a year is out someone blocks it and your mind turns elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 忠言者以信之不能終，頗自詘其謀，以為無益，此命令數更之弊也。

translations.literal: Those who speak loyal words, seeing that trust cannot last to the end, quite diminish their own plans as useless—this is the ill of orders changing frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Men of loyal counsel, seeing that trust cannot hold to the end, quietly set aside their plans as futile—this is the harm of commands that change too often.

sentences.zh: 夫爵賞，陛下所持之柄也。

translations.literal: Ranks and rewards are the handle Your Majesty holds.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and reward are the lever Your Majesty holds.

sentences.zh: 近時外戚、內臣以及士人，或因緣以求恩澤，從中而下謂之「內降」。

translations.literal: Recently consorts' kin, inner attendants, and scholars have sought grace through connections; from the center downward these are called "internal decrees."
translations.idiomatic: Of late consorts' kin, palace attendants, and literati have sought favor through connections; from the palace downward such appointments are called "inner promotions."

sentences.zh: 臣聞唐氏政衰，或母后專制，或妃主擅朝，樹恩私黨，名為「斜封」。

translations.literal: I hear that when Tang governance declined, sometimes an empress dowager monopolized rule or an imperial consort dominated the court, planting private factions of favor—this was called "oblique sealing."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that as Tang governance declined, empresses dowager or favored consorts at times seized the court, heaping private patronage on their factions—what was called "slant appointment."

sentences.zh: 今陛下威柄自出，外戚、內臣賢而才者，當與大臣公議而進之，何必襲「斜封」之弊哉。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's awesome handle issues from yourself; for worthy and talented consorts' kin and inner attendants, you should advance them after public discussion with great ministers—why must you inherit the ill of "oblique sealing"?
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty's authority proceeds from yourself; for worthy and able consorts' kin and palace attendants, you should promote them only after open deliberation with chief ministers—why repeat the abuse of slant appointment?

sentences.zh: 且使大臣從之，則壞陛下綱紀；

translations.literal: And if you make great ministers follow, you spoil Your Majesty's regulations;
translations.idiomatic: If you make chief ministers go along, you wreck Your Majesty's discipline;

sentences.zh: 不從，則沮陛下德音。

translations.literal: if they do not follow, they block Your Majesty's virtuous pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: if they refuse, they thwart Your Majesty's gracious edicts.

sentences.zh: 壞綱紀，忠臣所不忍為；

translations.literal: To spoil regulations—loyal ministers cannot bear to do it;
translations.idiomatic: To wreck discipline—loyal ministers cannot bring themselves to do it;

sentences.zh: 沮德音，則威柄輕於上。

translations.literal: to block virtuous pronouncements is to make the awesome handle light above.
translations.idiomatic: to thwart gracious edicts is to make authority light at the top.

sentences.zh: 且盡公不阿，朝廷所以責大臣。

translations.literal: Moreover, to be wholly public and not partial—this is what the court demands of great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to be wholly impartial—this is what the court demands of its chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 今乃自以私昵撓之，而欲責大臣之不私，難矣。

translations.literal: Now you yourself bend them with private favor, yet wish to demand that great ministers be without partiality—difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now you yourself sway them with private ties, yet expect chief ministers to be impartial—that is hard indeed.

sentences.zh: 此恩寵過濫之弊也。

translations.literal: This is the ill of favor lavished excessively.
translations.idiomatic: This is the harm of favor poured out without measure.

sentences.zh: 夫賜予者，國家所以勤功也。

translations.literal: Grants are how the state rewards merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts are how the state rewards achievement.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，嬪御及伶官、太醫之屬，賜予過厚。

translations.literal: In recent years imperial consorts, performers, imperial physicians, and the like have received grants excessively thick.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years consorts, entertainers, court physicians, and the like have been granted rewards far too lavish.

sentences.zh: 民間傳言，內帑金帛，皆祖宗累朝積聚。

translations.literal: Popular rumor says the inner treasury's gold and silk were accumulated by the ancestors through successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor among the people says the palace treasury's gold and silk were hoarded by the ancestors through reign after reign.

sentences.zh: 陛下用之，不甚愛惜，今之所存無幾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty uses them without great care; little now remains.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spends them without much restraint; little now remains.

sentences.zh: 疏遠之人，誠不能知內府豐匱之數，但見取於民者日煩，即知畜於公帑者不厚。

translations.literal: Remote persons truly cannot know whether the inner palace is abundant or scarce, but when they see levies on the people grow daily burdensome, they know what is stored in the public treasury is not thick.
translations.idiomatic: Men far from court cannot know the palace coffers' true state, but when they see exactions from the people grow ever heavier, they know the public treasury is not full.

sentences.zh: 臣亦知國家自西方宿兵，用度浸廣，帑藏之積，未必悉為賜予所費，然下民不可家至而戶曉，獨見陛下行事感動爾。

translations.literal: Your subject also knows that since the state garrisoned troops in the west expenses have gradually broadened and treasury savings were not necessarily all spent on grants; yet the lower people cannot be told house by house—they only see Your Majesty's conduct and are moved.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant also knows that since troops were stationed in the west costs have risen and not every coin in the treasury went to gifts; yet the common people cannot be reached in every home—they judge only by what Your Majesty does.

sentences.zh: 往歲聞邊將王珪，以力戰賜金，則無不悅服；

translations.literal: In former years I heard that when the border general Wang Gui was granted gold for fierce fighting, none failed to rejoice and submit;
translations.idiomatic: Years ago, when the frontier general Wang Gui was rewarded with gold for hard fighting, all rejoiced and submitted;

sentences.zh: 或見優人所得過厚，則往往憤歎。

translations.literal: when they saw performers' gains excessively thick, they often sighed in anger.
translations.idiomatic: when they saw entertainers paid far too much, they often sighed in indignation.

sentences.zh: 人情不可不察，此賜予不節之弊也。

translations.literal: Popular feeling cannot go unexamined—this is the ill of grants without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment cannot be ignored—this is the harm of gifts without limit.

sentences.zh: 臣所論三事，皆人人所共知，近臣從諛而不言，以至今日。

translations.literal: The three matters your subject discusses are what everyone knows; close ministers followed flattery and would not speak—until today.
translations.idiomatic: The three points your servant raises are known to all; close advisers flattered and held their tongues—until now.

sentences.zh: 方今非獨四夷之為患，朝政日弊而陛下不寤，人心日危而陛下不知。

translations.literal: Today it is not only the four barbarians that are the trouble: court administration daily declines while Your Majesty does not awaken; popular hearts daily grow perilous while Your Majesty does not know.
translations.idiomatic: Today the trouble is not the barbarians alone: court governance rots day by day while Your Majesty does not wake; hearts among the people grow fearful day by day while Your Majesty does not see it.

sentences.zh: 故臣願先正於內，以正於外。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject wishes first to set right what is within, in order to set right what is without.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore your servant asks first to set the inner house in order, that the outer realm may follow.

sentences.zh: 然後忠謀漸進，紀綱漸舉，國用漸足，士心漸奮。

translations.literal: Then loyal plans will gradually advance, regulations gradually be raised, state revenue gradually suffice, and scholars' hearts gradually be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Then loyal counsel will advance step by step, discipline will rise, the treasury will fill, and the spirit of the scholar-officials will revive.

sentences.zh: 邊境之患，庶乎息矣。

translations.literal: The troubles of the border regions—perhaps then they will cease.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier troubles—perhaps then they may quiet.

sentences.zh: 惟深察秦、隋惡聞忠言所以亡，遠法漢主不諱危亂所以存，日親盛德，與民更始，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Only deeply examine how Qin and Sui, hating to hear loyal words, therefore perished; far follow how Han sovereigns, not shrinking from peril and disorder, therefore endured—daily draw near abundant virtue and make a new beginning with the people; then the realm will be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Only ponder deeply how Qin and Sui, refusing loyal counsel, were destroyed; take as your distant model how Han rulers, not fearing to name danger and ruin, endured—draw daily near true virtue and begin anew with the people; then the realm will be blessed indeed."

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong gladly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong received it with approval.

sentences.zh: 改太常丞、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and made magistrate of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以右司諫、知渭州兼領涇原路經略公事。

translations.literal: As Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat he was made magistrate of Wei Prefecture while concurrently heading the Jingyuan Circuit frontier commission.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat he governed Wei Prefecture and concurrently directed Jingyuan Circuit frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 會鄭戩為陝西四路都總管，遣劉滬、董士廉城水洛，以通秦、渭援兵。

translations.literal: When Zheng Xian was overall commander of Shaanxi's four circuits, he sent Liu Hu and Dong Shilian to fortify Shuiluo, to link Qin and Wei with relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Xian commanded all four Shaanxi circuits, he sent Liu Hu and Dong Shilian to build Shuiluo, opening a route for Qin and Wei relief forces.

sentences.zh: 洙以為前此屢困於賊者，正由城砦多而兵勢分也。

translations.literal: Zhu thought that the reason they had repeatedly been trapped by the enemy before was precisely that there were many fort stockades and military strength was divided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu held that past defeats came precisely from too many fortified posts and scattered forces.

sentences.zh: 今又益城，不可，奏罷之。

translations.literal: To add another fort now was impossible; he memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Another fort, he argued, must not be built; he memorialized to halt the project.

sentences.zh: 時戩已解四路。

translations.literal: At the time Xian had already been relieved of the four circuits.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xian had already left the four-circuit command.

sentences.zh: 而奏滬等督役如故。

translations.literal: Yet he still memorialized that Hu and the others should supervise the labor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still reported that Hu and the others were pressing the work as before.

sentences.zh: 洙不平，遣人再召滬，不至；

translations.literal: Zhu was displeased and sent men twice to summon Hu, but Hu did not come;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, angered, twice sent men to summon Hu, but Hu would not come;

sentences.zh: 命張忠往代之，又不受。

translations.literal: he ordered Zhang Zhong to go and replace him, but Hu again would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Zhang Zhong to replace him, but Hu again refused.

sentences.zh: 於是諭狄青械滬、士廉下吏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he instructed Di Qing to shackle Hu and Shilian and hand them to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Di Qing to seize Hu and Shilian in irons and deliver them to the courts.

sentences.zh: 戩論奏不已，卒徙洙慶州而城水洛。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized arguments without cease; in the end Zhu was transferred to Qing Prefecture while Shuiluo was fortified.
translations.idiomatic: Xian kept memorializing; in the end Zhu was moved to Qing Prefecture while Shuiluo was completed.

sentences.zh: 又徙晉州，遷起居舍人、直龍圖閣、知潞州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Jin Prefecture, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman, Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and magistrate of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved again to Jin Prefecture, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman, given direct access to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and made magistrate of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會士廉詣闕上書訟洙，詔遣御史劉湜就鞫，不得他罪。

translations.literal: When Shilian came to court and memorialized to sue Zhu, an edict sent Censor Liu Shi to investigate on the spot; no other crime was found.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilian reached court and accused Zhu, the throne sent Censor Liu Shi to investigate on site; no further offense was found.

sentences.zh: 而洙以部將孫用由軍校補邊，自京師貸息錢到官，亡以償。

translations.literal: But Zhu, because his subordinate Sun Yong had been transferred from army rank to the frontier, had borrowed on interest in the capital and, arriving at his post, had nothing with which to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu's officer Sun Yong, promoted from the ranks to frontier service, had borrowed at interest in the capital and, on reaching his post, could not repay.

sentences.zh: 洙惜其才可用，恐以犯法罷去，嘗假公使錢為償之，又以為嘗自貸，坐貶崇信軍節度副使，天下莫不以為湜文致之也。

translations.literal: Zhu, cherishing his talent as usable and fearing he would be dismissed for breaking the law, once borrowed public envoy funds to repay for him; this was also treated as Zhu having lent personally, and he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Chongxin Army—the realm all thought Shi had framed him with words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, valuing his ability and fearing dismissal for debt, once used public envoy funds to cover the loan; this was judged as personal lending on Zhu's part, and he was demoted to deputy commissioner of the Chongxin Army—all under heaven believed Shi had trapped him with words.

sentences.zh: 徙監均州酒稅，感疾，沿牒至南陽訪醫，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Transferred to supervise the wine tax of Jun Prefecture, he fell ill; following his dispatch he went to Nanyang to seek a physician and died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to oversee Jun Prefecture's wine tax, he fell ill; traveling under his orders to Nanyang for treatment, he died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，宰相韓琦為洙言，乃追復故官，及官其子構。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era Chancellor Han Qi spoke on Zhu's behalf; his former office was posthumously restored and his son Gou was given an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiayou, Chancellor Han Qi pleaded for him; his old rank was restored posthumously and his son Gou was given office.

sentences.zh: 洙內剛外和，博學有識度，尤深於《春秋》。

translations.literal: Zhu was inwardly firm and outwardly gentle, broad in learning and possessed of judgment, and especially deep in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was steel within and mild without, learned and discerning, and especially steeped in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 自唐末歷五代，文格卑弱。

translations.literal: From late Tang through the Five Dynasties the literary style was base and weak.
translations.idiomatic: From late Tang through the Five Dynasties literary style had grown feeble.

sentences.zh: 至宋初，柳開始為古文，洙與穆修復振起之。

translations.literal: In early Song Liu Kai first revived ancient-style prose; Zhu, with Mu Xiu, raised it up again.
translations.idiomatic: In early Song Liu Kai first revived the ancient prose; Zhu, with Mu Xiu, helped lift it once more.

sentences.zh: 其為文簡而有法，有集二十七卷。

translations.literal: His writing was concise yet had method; he left a collection of writings in twenty-seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was spare yet disciplined; he left collected works in twenty-seven juan.

sentences.zh: 自元昊不庭，洙未嘗不在兵間，故於西事尤練習。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao was unsubmissive, Zhu was never out of the armies; hence he was especially practiced in western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Hao's rebellion onward Zhu was always with the troops; he knew western affairs especially well.

sentences.zh: 其為兵制之說，述戰守勝敗，盡當時利害。

translations.literal: His discourse on military institutions, narrating defense, offense, victory, and defeat, fully matched the benefit and harm of the time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings on military organization—on defense, attack, victory, and defeat—captured the stakes of the day.

sentences.zh: 又欲訓土兵代戍卒，以減邊費，為禦戎長久之策，皆未及施為。

translations.literal: He also wished to train local militia to replace garrison troops and reduce frontier expense, as a long-term strategy against the barbarians—all of which had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed training local militia to replace frontier garrisons and cut border costs—a lasting policy against the enemy—none of which was ever enacted.

sentences.zh: 而元昊臣，洙亦去而得罪矣。

translations.literal: But Yuan Hao submitted, and Zhu also left office and met with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao submitted, Zhu too had left office and fallen into disgrace.

sentences.zh: 孫甫，字之翰，許州陽翟人。

translations.literal: Sun Fu, style name Zhihan, was a native of Yangzhai in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, courtesy name Zhihan, was a native of Yangzhai in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好學，日誦數千言，慕孫何為古文章。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and recited several thousand words daily; he admired Sun He for ancient-style essays.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved study, reciting thousands of words a day, and took Sun He as his model in ancient prose.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，得同學究出身，為蔡州汝陽縣主簿。

translations.literal: On first passing the jinshi examination he received the tong jinshi chushen degree and served as clerk of Runyang County in Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his first jinshi attempt he received the tong jinshi chushen degree and became clerk of Runyang County in Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再舉進士及第，為華州推官。

translations.literal: On a second jinshi attempt he passed with honors and became investigative officer of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On a second jinshi attempt he passed at the top and became investigative officer of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使李紘薦其材，遷大理寺丞、知絳州翼城縣。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Li Hong recommended his talent; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Yicheng in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Li Hong praised his ability; he was made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yicheng in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 杜衍辟為永興司錄，凡吏職，纖末皆倚辦甫。

translations.literal: Du Yan recruited him as recorder of Yongxing; for every clerical duty, however minute, he relied on Fu to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan took him on as recorder at Yongxing; for every clerical task, however small, he leaned on Fu.

sentences.zh: 甫曰：「待我以此，可以去矣。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "If you treat me with this, I can leave."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Treat me like this and I am done."

sentences.zh: 衍聞之，不復以小事屬甫。

translations.literal: When Yan heard this, he no longer entrusted small matters to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Yan stopped handing him petty chores.

sentences.zh: 衍與讌語，甫必引經以對，言天下賢俊，歷評其才性所長。

translations.literal: When Yan conversed at feasts, Fu always answered by citing the classics and spoke of the realm's worthy men, appraising each one's talent and nature.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan's table Fu always answered with classical citations and reviewed the realm's eminent men, weighing each man's gifts.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「吾辟屬官，得益友。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "In recruiting a subordinate I have gained a beneficial friend."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "In hiring a clerk I gained a true friend."

sentences.zh: 諸生亦多從甫學問。

translations.literal: Students also often followed Fu to study and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Students too often sought Fu for learning and debate.

sentences.zh: 徙知永昌縣，監益州交子務，再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Yongchang, supervised the Yizhou Jiaozi Bureau, and was again promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Yongchang, oversaw the Yizhou Jiaozi office, and was again promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 蜀用鐵錢，民苦轉貿重，故設法書紙代錢，以便市易。

translations.literal: Shu used iron cash; the people suffered because trade and transport were heavy, so a law was devised to write paper in place of cash to ease market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Shu used iron coin, which made commerce burdensome; the government therefore issued paper notes to ease trade.

sentences.zh: 轉運使以偽造交子多犯法，欲廢不用。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner, because forged jiaozi often broke the law, wished to abolish and stop using them.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner, seeing widespread forgery of jiaozi, wanted to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 甫曰：「交子可以偽造，錢亦可以私鑄，私鑄有犯，錢可廢乎？

translations.literal: Fu said, "Jiaozi can be forged; cash can also be privately cast—when private casting is an offense, can cash be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Jiaozi can be counterfeited, but coin can be illicitly cast too—when private casting is a crime, do we abolish coin?

sentences.zh: 但嚴治之，不當以小仁廢大利。」

translations.literal: Only govern it strictly; one should not, for a small kindness, abolish a great benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Enforce the law sternly; do not discard a great gain for a petty mercy."

sentences.zh: 後卒不能廢。

translations.literal: In the end they still could not abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they could not abolish it.

sentences.zh: 衍為樞密副使，薦於朝，授秘閣校理。

translations.literal: When Yan became Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs he recommended Fu to court, and Fu was appointed Collation Officer of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan became Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs he recommended Fu to court, and Fu was made Collation Officer of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔三館臣僚言事。

translations.literal: That year an edict called on members of the Three Institutes to speak on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict invited Three Institutes officials to address state affairs.

sentences.zh: 甫進十二事，按祖宗故實，校當世之治有所不逮者，論述以為諷諫，名《三聖政範》。

translations.literal: Fu advanced twelve points, comparing the ancestors' precedents and gauging where current governance fell short, discussing them as admonition; he titled it "Models of the Three Sagely Reigns."
translations.idiomatic: Fu submitted twelve proposals, measuring present rule against ancestral precedent wherever it fell short, and set them down as remonstrance in a work titled Models of the Three Sagely Reigns.

sentences.zh: 改右正言。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Rectifier of Speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Rectifier of Speech.

sentences.zh: 時河北降赤雪，河東地震五六年不止，甫推《洪範五行傳》及前代變驗，上疏曰：「赤雪者，赤眚也，人君舒緩之應。

translations.literal: Then red snow fell in Hebei and earthquakes in Hedong continued five or six years without cease; Fu extrapolated from the Hongfan Five Elements Treatise and former omens, and memorialized, saying, "Red snow is a red calamity—the response to a sovereign's laxity.
translations.idiomatic: Red snow then fell in Hebei and Hedong shook for five or six years without stop; Fu drew on the Hongfan Five Elements Treatise and past omens and wrote, "Red snow is a red portent—the sign of a ruler grown slack.

sentences.zh: 舒緩則政事弛，賞罰差，百官廢職，所以召亂也。

translations.literal: When lax, government slackens, rewards and punishments go awry, and the hundred offices neglect duty—thus disorder is summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Slackness loosens government, skews reward and punishment, and lets the bureaucracy neglect its charge—thus chaos is invited.

sentences.zh: 晉太康中，河陰降赤雪。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era of Jin, red snow fell in Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Taikang era red snow fell at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 時武帝怠於政事，荒宴後宮。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu was slack in government affairs and dissipated himself feasting in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu neglected government and squandered his days feasting in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 每見臣下，多道常事，不及經國遠圖，故招赤眚之怪，終致晉亂。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw his subjects he mostly spoke of routine matters and did not reach to governing the state with far-reaching plans; therefore he summoned the wonder of red calamity and in the end brought on Jin's disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When he met his ministers he spoke only of routine matters, never of far-reaching statecraft; thus the red portent appeared and Jin fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 地震者，陰之盛也。

translations.literal: Earthquake is the excess of yin.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquake is yin in excess.

sentences.zh: 陰之象，臣也，後宮也，四夷也。

translations.literal: The image of yin is ministers, the rear palace, and the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yin stands for ministers, the inner palace, and the outer barbarians.

sentences.zh: 三者不可過盛，過盛則陰為變而動矣。

translations.literal: These three cannot pass into excess; when they do, yin changes and stirs.
translations.idiomatic: None of the three may grow too strong; when they do, yin shifts and the earth moves.

sentences.zh: 忻州趙分，地震六年。

translations.literal: In the Zhao allotment of Xin Prefecture, earthquakes lasted six years.
translations.idiomatic: In Xin Prefecture's Zhao region the earth shook for six years.

sentences.zh: 每震，則有聲如雷，前代地震，未有如此之久者。

translations.literal: With each tremor there was a sound like thunder; in previous ages there had been earthquakes, but never one lasting so long.
translations.idiomatic: Each shock brought thunderous noise; no earlier earthquake on record had endured so long.

sentences.zh: 惟唐高宗本封於晉，及即位，晉州經歲地震。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Gaozong of Tang had originally been enfeoffed in Jin, and upon his accession Jin Prefecture suffered earthquakes year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Tang Gaozong, who had first been enfeoffed in Jin: once he took the throne, Jin Prefecture shook for a full year.

sentences.zh: 宰相張行成言，恐女謁用事，大臣陰謀，宜制於未萌。

translations.literal: The chief councilor Zhang Xingcheng said he feared women at court would wield power and great ministers would plot in secret, and that one ought to check these things before they sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zhang Xingcheng warned that palace women might seize power and senior ministers plot in the shadows, and urged curbing such trends before they took root.

sentences.zh: 其後武昭儀專恣，幾移唐祚。

translations.literal: Afterward Empress Wu Zetian monopolized power wantonly and nearly shifted the Tang mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Zhaoyi dominated the court and nearly overturned the Tang succession.

sentences.zh: 天地災變，固不虛應，陛下救紓緩之失，莫若自主威福，時出英斷，以懾姦邪，以肅天下。

translations.literal: Heaven-and-earth disasters and transformations surely do not respond in vain; to remedy Your Majesty's errors of lax indulgence, nothing surpasses holding authority and blessing in your own hands, issuing timely heroic decisions, to awe treacherous evil and to bring solemn order to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's omens are never empty warnings. To correct Your Majesty's habit of lenient delay, nothing beats reclaiming authority, acting decisively when needed, terrifying the wicked, and restoring order under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 救陰盛之變，莫若外謹戎備，內制後宮。

translations.literal: To remedy the transformation of yin in excess, nothing surpasses being strict in military readiness abroad and restraining the rear palace within.
translations.idiomatic: To answer yin's excess, guard the frontier abroad and control the inner palace at home.

sentences.zh: 謹戎備，則切責大臣，使之預圖兵防，熟計成敗；

translations.literal: In being strict in military readiness, then sternly charge the great ministers, causing them to plan defenses in advance and weigh success and failure thoroughly;
translations.idiomatic: For frontier readiness, rebuke your chief ministers until they plan defenses ahead and weigh every outcome;

sentences.zh: 制後宮，則凡掖庭非典掌御幸者，盡出之，且裁節其恩，使無過分，此應天之實也。」

translations.literal: in restraining the rear palace, then all in the inner quarters who are not of proper office charged with imperial favor should be sent out entirely, and moreover cut back their favors so they have no excess — this is the substance of responding to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: for the inner palace, remove every woman in the rear apartments who lacks proper title to the emperor's bed, and trim their privileges so none overstep — that is how one truly answers Heaven."

sentences.zh: 時契丹、西夏稍強，後宮張修媛寵幸，大臣專政，甫以此諫焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan and Western Xia were growing somewhat strong; in the rear palace Zhang Xiuyuan enjoyed favor; great ministers monopolized government — Fu offered these remonstrances on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans and Western Xia were gaining strength; Consort Zhang Xiuyuan held the emperor's favor; ministers ruled unchecked — it was for this that Fu spoke up.

sentences.zh: 又言：「修媛寵恣市恩，禍漸已萌。

translations.literal: He also said: "Xiuyuan, favored and wanton, trades favors in the market; disaster has already begun to sprout.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Xiuyuan abuses her favor to buy loyalty in the open; the harm has already begun to grow.

sentences.zh: 夫后者，正嫡也，其餘皆婢妾爾。

translations.literal: The empress is the legitimate wife; all others are but maidservants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The empress alone is the lawful consort; every other woman is merely a servant or concubine.

sentences.zh: 貴賤有等，用物不宜過僭。

translations.literal: Noble and base have their ranks; use of goods ought not to pass beyond what is proper.
translations.idiomatic: Rank has its limits; no woman's goods should exceed her station.

sentences.zh: 自古寵女色，初不制而後不能制者，其禍不可悔。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity those who favored women's beauty and at first did not restrain them but afterward could not restrain them — their disasters cannot be regretted away."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, rulers who indulged beauty without restraint until restraint was impossible have suffered irreversible ruin."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「用物在有司，朕恨不知爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Use of goods lies with the responsible offices; We regret not having known this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The responsible offices control such matters; I regret I did not know."

sentences.zh: 甫曰：「世謂諫臣耳目官，所以達不知也。

translations.literal: Fu said: "The world calls remonstrating officials the eyes and ears of office — that is how what is unknown is conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu answered: "People call remonstrators the ruler's eyes and ears — our office exists to tell you what you do not know.

sentences.zh: 若所謂前世女禍者，載在書史，陛下可自知也。」

translations.literal: As for what are called the disasters of women in former ages, they are recorded in books and histories; Your Majesty can know them for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: As for the womanly calamities of past dynasties, they fill the histories; Your Majesty may read them for yourself."

sentences.zh: 夏國乞盟，甫上一利四害，曰：「宿兵以來，國用空耗。

translations.literal: When the Xia state begged for alliance, Fu submitted one benefit and four harms, saying: "Since troops were long stationed, state expenditures have been emptied.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Xia sought peace, Fu presented one gain and four losses: "Since we began keeping troops in the field, the treasury has been drained.

sentences.zh: 今若與之約和，則邊兵可減，科斂可省。

translations.literal: Now if we make a treaty of peace with them, then frontier troops can be reduced and levies and collections can be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If we treaty with them now, we can cut frontier garrisons and lighten taxes.

sentences.zh: 其為利一也。

translations.literal: This is the first benefit.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first gain.

sentences.zh: 始，契丹聲言，嘗遣使諭西人使臣中國。

translations.literal: At the beginning the Khitan proclaimed that they had once sent envoys to instruct the western people to submit as ministers to China.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitans boasted that they had once sent envoys to persuade the Western Xia to submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 今和議既成，必恃其功。

translations.literal: Now that the peace agreement is concluded, they are sure to rely on this achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace is settled, they will surely claim credit for it.

sentences.zh: 去歲有割地之請，朝廷已增歲賂，若更有求，將安拒之？

translations.literal: Last year there was a request to cede territory; the court already increased the annual tribute; if they seek more, how will we refuse them?
translations.idiomatic: Last year they asked for land; we already raised the annual gift. If they demand more, how shall we refuse?

sentences.zh: 其為害一也。

translations.literal: This is the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first loss.

sentences.zh: 自承平四十年，武事不飭，及邊鄙有警，而用不習之將，不練之兵，故久無成功。

translations.literal: Since forty years of sustained peace, military affairs were not put in order; when the borderlands had alarms, untrained generals and unpracticed troops were used — therefore for long there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years of peace left our armies neglected; when the frontier alarmed, we sent untrained generals and raw troops — hence our long failure.

sentences.zh: 然比來邊臣中材謀勇健者，往往復出，方在講訓不懈，以張中國之威。

translations.literal: Yet of late among frontier officials those of middling talent, strategy, courage, and vigor have often reappeared; they are just now in unceasing drill and instruction, to extend China's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately capable, bold frontier officers have reappeared and drill without slackening to restore China's prestige.

sentences.zh: 一旦因議和弛備，復如曩日，緩急必不可用。

translations.literal: Once because of peace talks readiness is relaxed, again as in former days — in urgency they certainly cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: If we relax defenses for peace talks, we will be as helpless as before when crisis comes.

sentences.zh: 其為害二也。

translations.literal: This is the second harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second loss.

sentences.zh: 自元昊拒命，終不敢深入關中者，以唃廝囉等族不附，慮為後患也。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao defied the command, in the end he did not dare penetrate deeply into Guanzhong because the Gusiluo clans and others did not attach themselves, and he feared them as a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao rebelled he never dared drive deep into Guanzhong, fearing the Gusiluo tribes and others who had not submitted would strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 今中國與之和，獲歲遺之厚，彼必專力以制二蕃，強大之勢，自茲為始。

translations.literal: Now that China makes peace with them and obtains thick annual gifts, they are sure to concentrate their strength to subdue the two fan states; the momentum of growing strong begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: Once we treat with them and pay rich yearly gifts, they will turn their full strength on the two Tibetan powers — their rise begins here.

sentences.zh: 其為害三也。

translations.literal: This is the third harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third loss.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷恃久安之勢，法令紀綱，弛而不葺。

translations.literal: Moreover the court relies on the momentum of long peace; laws, ordinances, and discipline are relaxed and not repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the court rests on long peace; statutes and discipline sag unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 及西戎累敗，王師始議更張，以救前弊。

translations.literal: When the western barbarians were repeatedly defeated, the royal army at last deliberated on renewal, to rescue former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Only after repeated defeats of the Western Xia did the court begin to reform and remedy old abuses.

sentences.zh: 今見戎人請和，苟貪無事，他時之患，不可救矣。

translations.literal: Now seeing the Rong people request peace, if we greedily seek no trouble, the disaster of another time cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If we grasp at peace because the barbarians sue for it, future calamity will be beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 其為害四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth loss.

sentences.zh: 凡利害之機，願陛下熟圖之。」

translations.literal: In all, the pivot of benefit and harm — may Your Majesty ponder it thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: On every point of gain and loss, I beg Your Majesty to weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 又言：「張子奭使夏州回，元昊復稱臣，然乞歲賣青鹽十萬石，兼欲就京師互市諸物，仍求增歲給之數。

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhang Zishi, returning from his mission to Xia Prefecture, reported that Yuan Hao again styled himself a minister, yet begged to sell one hundred thousand piculs of green salt annually, and moreover wished to trade various goods at the capital, still seeking to increase the number of annual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Zhang Zishi returned from Xia Prefecture reporting that Yuan Hao again calls himself our subject, yet asks to sell one hundred thousand piculs of green salt yearly, trade at the capital, and raise his annual stipend.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂西鹽數萬石，其直不下錢十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that several tens of thousands of piculs of western salt — their value is not less than more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon tens of thousands of piculs of Western salt are worth no less than a hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 況朝廷已許歲賜二十五萬，若又許其賣鹽，則與遺契丹物數相當。

translations.literal: Moreover the court has already granted an annual gift of two hundred fifty thousand; if we also permit them to sell salt, then it equals the quantity of goods given to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: We already grant them two hundred fifty thousand a year; if we also let them sell salt, our gift to Western Xia will match what we give the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 使契丹聞之，則貪得之心生矣。

translations.literal: If the Khitan hear of it, then the heart of greedy gain will arise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans hear of it, their greed will awaken.

sentences.zh: 況自德明之時，累乞放行青鹽，先帝以其亂法，不聽。

translations.literal: Moreover from the time of Deming they repeatedly begged to release green salt; the former emperor, because it would disorder the law, did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Deming's day they have repeatedly asked to sell green salt; the late emperor refused, lest it break the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 及請之不已，追德明弟入質而許之，是則以彼難從之事，杜其意也。

translations.literal: When they asked without cease, Deming's younger brother was compelled to enter as hostage and then it was granted — this was using what was hard for them to comply with, to block their intent.
