translations.idiomatic: When they would not stop asking, the court demanded Deming's brother as hostage before consenting — a hard condition meant to shut down the request.

sentences.zh: 蓋鹽，中國之大利，又西戎之鹽，味勝解池所出，而出產無窮。

translations.literal: For salt is China's great profit; moreover the salt of the western Rong surpasses in flavor what comes from the Jiechi ponds, and its output is inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: Salt is one of China's greatest revenues; Western salt tastes better than Jiechi salt and flows without end.

sentences.zh: 既開其禁，則流於民間，無以堤防矣。

translations.literal: Once its prohibition is opened, then it flows among the people and cannot be diked and defended.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ban is lifted, salt will flood the people and we cannot contain it.

sentences.zh: 兼聞張子奭言，元昊自拒命以來，收結人心，鈔掠所得，旋給其眾，兵力雖勝，用度隨窘。

translations.literal: Moreover I heard Zhang Zishi say that since Yuan Hao defied the command, he has gathered and bound hearts; what was seized by plunder he immediately gives to his masses; though military strength wins, expenditures follow into straits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zishi also reports that since his rebellion Yuan Hao has won loyalty and paid loot straight to his troops; his armies win battles but his treasury grows tight.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，尤宜以計困之，安得汲汲與和，曲徇其請乎？」

translations.literal: At such a time as this, it is especially fitting to use stratagem to distress them — how can we hurry to make peace and bend to follow their requests?"
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment to wear him down by policy — how can we rush to peace and indulge every demand?"

sentences.zh: 時陝西經略招討副使韓琦、判官尹洙還朝，甫建議請詔琦等，條四路將官能否，為上、中、下三等，黜其最下者。

translations.literal: At that time Shaanxi frontier pacification and recruitment Vice Commissioner Han Qi and judicial aide Yin Zhu returned to court; Fu proposed requesting an edict to Qi and the others to list the ability of generals and officers on the four circuits as upper, middle, and lower thirds, and dismiss the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi, Vice Commissioner for Shaanxi frontier affairs, and Yin Zhu, his judicial aide, returned to court, Fu urged the emperor to rank every general on the four frontier circuits as superior, middling, or inferior, and dismiss the worst.

sentences.zh: 保州兵變前，有告者，大臣不時發之。

translations.literal: Before the Baozhou troop mutiny there was one who reported it; the great ministers did not issue [action] in time.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Baozhou mutiny someone warned the court, but the chief ministers did not act in time.

sentences.zh: 甫因言樞密使副當得罪，使，乃杜衍也。

translations.literal: Fu therefore said the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs ought to bear guilt; the commissioner was Du Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then said the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs should be punished — the commissioner was Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 邊將劉滬城水洛於渭州，總管尹洙以滬違節度，將斬之。

translations.literal: The frontier general Liu Hu fortified Shuiluo in Weizhou; the overall commander Yin Zhu, because Hu violated command and discipline, was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier general Liu Hu built a fort at Shuiluo in Weizhou; overall commander Yin Zhu, citing disobedience, prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 大臣稍主洙議，甫以謂：「水洛通秦、渭，於國家為利，滬不可罪。」

translations.literal: The great ministers mostly sided with Yin Zhu's proposal; Fu held that "Shuiluo connects Qin and Wei — it is a benefit to the state; Hu cannot be guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers backed Yin Zhu; Fu argued that "Shuiluo links Qin and Wei and serves the state — Liu Hu must not be punished."

sentences.zh: 由是罷洙而釋滬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin Zhu was dismissed and Hu was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu was removed and Liu Hu freed.

sentences.zh: 衍屢薦甫，洙與甫素善者，而甫不少假借，其鯁亮不私如此。

translations.literal: Du Yan repeatedly recommended Fu; Yin Zhu and Fu had long been on good terms — yet Fu did not grant the least indulgence; his stern integrity and lack of partiality were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan had often recommended Fu; Yin Zhu was Fu's friend — yet Fu showed no favoritism; such was his upright, impartial character.

sentences.zh: 甫嘗言參知政事陳執中不學亡術，不可用。

translations.literal: Fu once said that Participation Councilor Chen Zhizhong was unlearned and devoid of method, and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Fu once declared that Vice Councilor Chen Zhizhong was ignorant and without ability, and unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 帝難之，由是求補外，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor found it difficult; on that account [Fu] sought an outside appointment, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demurred; Fu then asked to leave the capital, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 其後奏丁度因對求進用，帝曰：「度未嘗請也。」

translations.literal: Afterward he memorialized that Ding Du, in replying to an audience, sought advancement; the emperor said: "Du never requested it."
translations.idiomatic: Later he reported that Ding Du had sought promotion during an audience; the emperor said, "Du never asked."

sentences.zh: 度乞與甫辯，且指甫為宰相杜衍門人。

translations.literal: Ding Du begged to debate with Fu, and moreover pointed to Fu as a follower of Chief Councilor Du Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Du demanded a public debate and called Fu a protégé of Chief Councilor Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 乃以右司諫出知鄧州，徙安州，歷江東、兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Right Remonstrator of the Right Bureau to know Deng Prefecture, transferred to An Prefecture, and served successively as transport commissioner for Jiangdong and the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Right Remonstrator and sent to govern Deng, then An, and later served as transport commissioner for Jiangdong and the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 范仲俺知杭州，多以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, knowing Hangzhou, often acted largely at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan governed Hangzhou and often acted on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 甫曰：「范公，大臣也。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Lord Fan is a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "Lord Fan is a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 吾屈於此，則不得伸於彼矣。」

translations.literal: If I yield here, then I cannot stand firm there."
translations.idiomatic: If I bend here, I cannot hold firm there."

sentences.zh: 一切繩之以法，然退未嘗不稱其賢。

translations.literal: He bound everything to the law, yet on retiring he never failed to praise Fan's worth.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law without exception, yet in private never failed to praise Fan's virtue.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書兵部員外郎，改直史館、知陝州，徙晉州。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of War of the Department of State Affairs, changed to Direct Historian of the Historiography Institute and to know Shaan Prefecture, and moved to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted twice to Vice Director of the Ministry of War, made Direct Historian and prefect of Shaan, then transferred to Jin.

sentences.zh: 為河東轉運使、三司度支副使，遷刑部郎中、天章閣待制、河北都轉運使，留為侍讀。

translations.literal: He served as Hedong transport commissioner and Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the State Finance Commission, was transferred to Director of Punishments in the Ministry of Justice, Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion, and Chief Transport Commissioner for Hebei; he was retained as Imperial Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hedong transport commissioner and Vice Commissioner of Revenue, then Director of Punishments, Hanlin Academician of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion, and Chief Transport Commissioner for Hebei, and was kept at court as Imperial Reader.

sentences.zh: 卒，特贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On his death he was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 甫性勁果，善持論，有文集七卷，著《唐史記》七十五卷。

translations.literal: Fu's nature was forceful and resolute; he was skilled at holding to argument; he had a collection of writings in seven juan and authored Records of Tang History in seventy-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was firm and decisive, a powerful debater, author of seven juan of collected works and seventy-five juan of Records of Tang History.

sentences.zh: 每言唐君臣行事，以推見當時治亂，若身履其間，而聽者曉然，如目見之。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Tang ruler-and-subject conduct, he used it to infer the order and disorder of that time, as if he himself walked in their midst; listeners understood clearly, as if seeing with the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When he discussed Tang rulers and ministers, he made their age's rise and fall vivid, as though he had lived through it; listeners understood as if they saw it themselves.

sentences.zh: 時人言：「終日讀史，不如一日聽孫論也。」

translations.literal: Men of the time said: "Reading history all day is not equal to one day listening to Sun's discourse."
translations.idiomatic: People said: "A whole day reading history is worth less than an hour hearing Sun Fu speak."

sentences.zh: 《唐史》藏秘閣。

translations.literal: The Tang History was stored in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: His Tang History was deposited in the imperial Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 謝絳，字希深，其先陽夏人。

translations.literal: Xie Jiang, style name Xishen — his ancestors were men of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jiang, courtesy name Xishen, came originally from Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 祖懿文，為杭州鹽官縣令，葬富陽，遂為富陽人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yiwen served as magistrate of Yanguan County in Hangzhou; he was buried in Fuyang, and thus they became men of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yiwen was magistrate of Yanguan in Hangzhou; buried at Fuyang, the family henceforth counted as Fuyang people.

sentences.zh: 父濤，以文行稱，進士起家，為梓州榷鹽院判官。

translations.literal: His father Tao was famed for literary conduct; he entered office through the jinshi and served as judicial aide of the Zizhou Salt Monopoly Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was known for learning and integrity, a jinshi who served as judicial aide at the Zizhou salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 李順反成都，攻陷州縣，濤嘗畫守禦之計。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled at Chengdu and captured prefectures and counties, Tao once drew up plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled in Chengdu and overran the region, Tao drafted plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功遷觀察推官，權知華陽縣。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, for merit he was transferred to observation push officer and acted as magistrate of Huayang County.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed he was promoted to observation push officer and acting magistrate of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 亂亡之後，田廬荒廢，詔有能占田而倍入租者與之，於是腴田悉為豪右所占，流民至無所歸。

translations.literal: After the chaos and ruin, fields and dwellings lay waste; an edict said that whoever could occupy fields and pay double rent would receive them — thus fertile fields were all occupied by powerful families, and displaced people came even to having nowhere to return.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion fields lay waste; the throne promised land to anyone who would farm it and pay double rent, so the gentry seized the best fields and refugees had nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 濤收詔書，悉以田還主。

translations.literal: Tao collected the edicts and wholly returned the fields to their owners.
translations.idiomatic: Tao gathered the edicts and returned every field to its rightful owner.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省著作佐郎、知興國軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Assistant in the Palace Library and to know Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant in the Palace Library and military commissioner of Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 還，以治行召對長春殿，命試學士院。

translations.literal: On his return, for administrative conduct he was summoned to audience in the Changchun Hall and ordered to take the Hanlin examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled for his record of governance, he was summoned to the Changchun Hall and examined for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入寇，真宗議親征，時曹、濮多盜，而契丹聲言趨齊、鄆，以濤知曹州。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan entered to raid; Emperor Zhenzong deliberated on a personal campaign; at the time Cao and Pu had many bandits, while the Khitan proclaimed they were hurrying toward Qi and Yun — Tao was appointed to know Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded and Zhenzong considered leading the army in person, Cao and Pu were rife with bandits and the Khitans threatened Qi and Yun — Tao was sent to govern Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬縣賦稅多輸睢陽助兵食，是歲霖潦，百姓苦於轉送，濤悉留不遣。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties' tax levies were mostly forwarded to Suiyang to aid army provisions; that year there were heavy rains and floods, and the people suffered from transport — Tao wholly retained them and did not send them.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties had been shipping taxes to Suiyang for the army; floods that year made transport unbearable, and Tao kept every levy in place.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「江、淮漕運，日過睢陽，可取以餉軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "The Jiang-Huai grain transport passes Suiyang daily; it can be taken to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Grain from Jiang and Huai passes Suiyang daily and can supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 願留曹賦繇廣濟河以饋京師。」

translations.literal: I beg to retain Cao's levies and route them by the Guangji Canal to feed the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Let Cao's taxes stay here and send them to the capital by the Guangji Canal instead."

sentences.zh: 轉運使論以為不可，詔從濤奏。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner argued that it could not be done; an edict followed Tao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner objected, but the throne approved Tao's plan.

sentences.zh: 嘗使蜀還，舉所部官三十餘人。

translations.literal: Once, returning from a mission to Shu, he recommended more than thirty officials of his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from a mission to Shu, he recommended more than thirty subordinates.

sentences.zh: 宰相疑以為多，濤曰：「有罪，願連坐之。」

translations.literal: The chief councilor suspected the number was too many; Tao said: "If there is guilt, I wish to be punished together with them."
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor thought the list too long; Tao said: "If any are guilty, punish me with them."

sentences.zh: 奉使舉官連坐，自濤始。

translations.literal: Joint responsibility for envoys' recommendations began with Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Joint liability for envoys' nominees began with Tao.

sentences.zh: 久之，用馮拯薦，復召試，以尚書兵部員外郎直史館，遂兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: After long service, on Feng Zheng's recommendation he was again summoned for examination, made Vice Director in the Ministry of War with direct appointment in the Historiography Institute, and then also concurrently Palace Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Feng Zheng's recommendation, he was examined again, made Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Direct Historian, and then also Palace Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 真宗山陵靈駕所經道路，有司請悉壞城門、廬舍，以過車輿象物。

translations.literal: On the road the imperial catafalque for Zhenzong's mountain tomb would pass, the responsible offices requested to destroy all city gates and dwellings entirely, so that the carriage, chariots, and ritual objects might pass.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhenzong's tomb procession the authorities asked to tear down every city gate and house along the route so the imperial carriage and ritual gear could pass.

sentences.zh: 濤言：「先帝車駕封祀，儀物大備，猶不聞有所毀撤，且遺詔從儉薄。

translations.literal: Tao said: "When the late emperor's carriage went on the Feng and Shan sacrifices, ritual objects were greatly complete, yet one never heard of anything being destroyed and removed; moreover the testamentary edict followed frugal simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Tao argued: "When the late emperor traveled for the Feng and Shan rites, his equipage was magnificent, yet nothing was torn down; besides, his testament urged frugality.

sentences.zh: 今有司治明器侈大，以勞州縣，非先帝意，願下少府裁損之。」

translations.literal: Now the responsible offices prepare burial objects extravagantly large, to weary prefectures and counties — this is not the late emperor's intent; I beg that the Imperial Workshop be ordered to cut and reduce them."
translations.idiomatic: Now officials are building oversized burial goods that burden the provinces — this betrays the late emperor's will; let the Imperial Workshop scale them back."

sentences.zh: 進直昭文館，累官至太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Direct Appointment in the Zhaowen Hall and rose in office to Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Appointment in the Zhaowen Hall and rose to Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 絳以父任試秘書省校書郎，舉進士中甲科，授太常寺奉禮郎、知汝陰縣。

translations.literal: Jiang entered office through his father's position, tried as collator in the Secretariat, passed the jinshi in the top grade, and was appointed Ceremonial Officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Ruyin County.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang entered service by his father's rank, tried as a Secretariat collator, took the jinshi in the top grade, and became Ceremonial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 善議論，喜談時事，嘗論四民失業，累數千言。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discourse, fond of discussing current affairs; he once discussed the four classes losing their occupations in several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He debated well and loved current affairs; once he wrote thousands of words on how the four estates were losing their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，上疏謂宋當以土德王天下。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era he submitted a memorial holding that Song ought to take the Earth Virtue to rule all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianxi he memorialized that Song should rule under the virtue of Earth.

sentences.zh: 時大理寺丞董行父，請用天為統，以金為德。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Xingfu, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review, requested using Heaven as the succession and Metal as the virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Then Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Dong Xingfu proposed Heaven as the cosmic cycle and Metal as the dynasty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 詔兩制議，皆言：「用土德，則當越唐上承於隋；

translations.literal: An edict ordered deliberation by the Two Academies; all said: "Using Earth Virtue, then one ought to leap over Tang and inherit upward from Sui;
translations.idiomatic: The Two Academies were ordered to debate; all said: "With Earth as our virtue we must skip Tang and inherit from Sui;

sentences.zh: 用金德，則當越五代紹唐。

translations.literal: using Metal Virtue, then one ought to leap over the Five Dynasties and continue Tang.
translations.idiomatic: with Metal we must skip the Five Dynasties and continue Tang.

sentences.zh: 而太祖實受終周室，豈可弗遵傳繼之序？」

translations.literal: Yet the Taizu in fact received the mandate from the Zhou house — how can one fail to follow the order of transmitted succession?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taizu truly took the throne from Zhou — how can we ignore the order of succession?"

sentences.zh: 絳、行父議皆黜不用。

translations.literal: The proposals of Jiang and Xingfu were both dismissed and not used.
translations.idiomatic: The views of Jiang and Xingfu were both rejected.

sentences.zh: 楊億薦絳文章，召試，擢秘閣校理、同判太常禮院。

translations.literal: Yang Yi recommended Jiang's writings; he was summoned for examination, selected as collator in the Palace Library, and made Associate Judge of the Court of Imperial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi praised Jiang's writing; summoned for examination, he was made Palace Library collator and Associate Judge of the Court of Imperial Rites.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，仁宗即位，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended, Renzong took the throne, and he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, when the mourning ended and Renzong ascended, he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 用鄭氏《經》、唐故事議宣祖非受命祖，不宜配享感生帝，請以真宗配之。

translations.literal: Using the Zheng clan Classic and Tang precedents, he argued that Emperor Xuanzu was not the founder who received the Mandate and ought not be paired in sacrifice with the Spirit-Generator Emperor; he asked that Emperor Zhenzong be paired instead.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the Zheng clan Classic and Tang precedent, he argued that Emperor Xuanzu was not the dynastic founder who received Heaven's mandate and should not share sacrifice with the Spirit-Generator Emperor, and proposed pairing Emperor Zhenzong instead.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨李維以為不可。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief Li Wei held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, Expositor-in-Chief among the Hanlin Academicians, said it could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 尋出通判常州。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as administrative vice-prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted out as vice-prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，天下水旱、蝗起，河決滑州，絳上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, flood and drought afflicted the realm, locusts arose, and the Yellow River burst its banks at Huazhou; Jiang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: During Tiansheng, floods and drought struck the empire, locusts appeared, and the Yellow River broke through at Huazhou. Jiang memorialized the throne:

sentences.zh: 「去年京師大水，敗民廬舍，河渠暴溢，幾冒城郭；

translations.literal: "Last year the capital suffered great flood; it destroyed the people's houses, rivers and canals surged over their banks, and nearly engulfed the city walls;
translations.idiomatic: "Last year the capital was inundated. Homes were wrecked, rivers and canals burst their banks, and the flood nearly overtopped the walls;

sentences.zh: 今年苦旱，百姓疫死，田穀焦槁，秋成絕望：此皆大異也。

translations.literal: this year severe drought; the people die of pestilence, fields and grain are scorched dry, and the autumn harvest is despaired of: all these are great anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: this year brings cruel drought: the people perish of plague, grain withers in the fields, and the autumn harvest is hopeless—all great portents.

sentences.zh: 按《洪範》、京房《易傳》皆以為簡祭祀，逆天時，則水不順下；

translations.literal: According to the Great Plan and Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes, all hold that simplifying sacrifices and defying Heaven's seasons makes water fail to flow downward;
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan and Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes both teach that when sacrifices are curtailed and Heaven's seasons are defied, water will not run down as it should;

sentences.zh: 政令逆時，水失其性，則壞國邑，傷稼穡；

translations.literal: when government orders oppose the season and water loses its nature, then states and cities are ruined and crops harmed;
translations.idiomatic: when edicts run against the season and water loses its proper nature, states and towns are ruined and the harvest is harmed;

sentences.zh: 顓事者知，誅罰絕理，則大水殺人；

translations.literal: when those who monopolize affairs are knowing yet punishments sever all reason, then great flood kills the people;
translations.idiomatic: when power is monopolized by the knowing yet punishments cut off all reason, great flood takes human lives;

sentences.zh: 欲德不用，茲謂張，厥災荒；

translations.literal: when virtue is not employed, this is called "spread," and its disaster is famine;
translations.idiomatic: when virtue goes unused, this is called "spread," and its calamity is famine;

sentences.zh: 上下皆蔽，茲謂隔，其咎旱：天道指類示戒，大要如此。

translations.literal: when above and below are all blocked, this is called "barrier," and its fault is drought: Heaven's Way points to categories and shows warnings—the great purport is thus.
translations.idiomatic: when above and below are shut off, this is called "barrier," and its blame is drought: Heaven's Way names the type and sends warning—the gist is just this.

sentences.zh: 陛下夙夜勤苦，思有以上塞時變，固宜策告殃咎，變更理化，下罪己之詔，修順時之令，宣群言以導壅，斥近幸以損陰。

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils diligently day and night, thinking to plug the seasonal changes from above; you ought indeed to report the calamities and faults, transform and renew civil order, issue an edict blaming yourself, repair orders that accord with the seasons, give voice to all counsel to unblock obstruction, and drive off intimate favorites to diminish yin.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty labors day and night, seeking from above to answer the seasons' change; you should proclaim the disasters and faults, renew civil order, issue a self-reproach edict, restore timely ordinances, open all counsel to clear blockage, and dismiss close favorites to reduce yin.

sentences.zh: 而聖心優柔，重在改作，號令所發，未聞有以當天心者。

translations.literal: Yet the sagely heart is tender and hesitant, stressing costly reforms; of orders issued, none are heard that hit Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial heart is gentle and slow, weighting grand reforms; among commands issued, none are heard to match Heaven's mind.

sentences.zh: 夫風雨、寒暑之於天時，為大信也；

translations.literal: Wind, rain, cold, and heat in Heaven's seasons are the great trust;
translations.idiomatic: Wind, rain, cold, and heat in the heavenly seasons are the supreme pledge;

sentences.zh: 信不及於物，澤不究於下，則水旱為沴。

translations.literal: when trust does not reach things and bounty does not penetrate below, then flood and drought become baleful visitations.
translations.idiomatic: when the pledge fails to reach things and favor does not soak the realm below, flood and drought become harms.

sentences.zh: 近日制命，有信宿輒改，適行遽止，而欲風雨以信，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Recently edicts have been changed after barely a night, set forth only to be halted at once—yet you wish wind and rain to be trusted: can it be had?
translations.idiomatic: Lately decrees are altered within a night, promulgated only to be stopped at once—yet you expect wind and rain to keep faith: how can that be?

sentences.zh: 天下之廣，萬幾之眾，不出房闥，豈能盡知？

translations.literal: The realm is vast and myriad affairs numerous; if they do not leave the inner chambers, how can all be known?
translations.idiomatic: The empire is wide and affairs beyond counting; if they never leave the inner quarters, how can you know them all?

sentences.zh: 而在廷之臣，未聞被數刻之召，吐片言之善，朝夕左右，非恩澤即佞幸，上下皆蔽，其應不虛。

translations.literal: Yet among ministers at court none are heard summoned for an hour's audience to speak a word of good counsel; those at your side morning and evening are either recipients of favor or flatterers—above and below all blocked, and the response is not empty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court no minister is summoned for even an hour to offer a scrap of good counsel; those who attend you dawn to dusk are either favorites or flatterers—above and below shut off, and the omen is no empty sign.

sentences.zh: 昔兩漢日食、地震、水旱之變，則策免三公，以示戒懼。

translations.literal: In former Han times, at changes of solar eclipse, earthquake, flood, and drought, they demoted the Three Excellencies by imperial rescript to show caution and fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the two Han dynasties, at eclipses, earthquakes, floods, and droughts, they removed the Three Excellencies by rescript to show alarm.

sentences.zh: 陛下進用丞弼，極一時之選，而政道未茂，天時未順，豈大臣輔佐不明邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has promoted chancellors chosen as the best of the age, yet the way of government is not lush and Heaven's seasons are not compliant—are the great ministers' aid unclear?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has advanced chancellors picked as the finest of the time, yet government does not flourish and the seasons do not obey—are your ministers' counsel unclear?

sentences.zh: 陛下信任不篤邪？

translations.literal: Or Your Majesty's trust not deep?
translations.idiomatic: Or Your Majesty's trust not firm?

sentences.zh: 必若使之，宜推心責成，以極其效；

translations.literal: If you will employ them, you should open your heart, charge them with responsibility, and bring their effect to the utmost;
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to use them, lay your heart open, charge them with full responsibility, and demand their utmost;

sentences.zh: 謂之不然，則更選賢者。

translations.literal: if you deem otherwise, then choose worthier men anew.
translations.idiomatic: if not, choose worthier men again.

sentences.zh: 比來姦邪者易進，守道者數窮，政出多門，俗喜由徑。

translations.literal: Lately the wicked and crooked are easily advanced while those who hold the Way are repeatedly ruined; government issues from many gates and custom delights in shortcuts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the wicked rise easily while men of the Way are often ruined; policy comes from many doors and the people love bypaths.

sentences.zh: 聖心固欲盡得天下之賢能，分職受業；

translations.literal: The sagely heart surely wishes to gain all worthies under Heaven and divide offices and receive their teachings;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial heart surely seeks every worthy under Heaven, dividing offices and receiving their service;

sentences.zh: 而宰相方考賢進吏，無敢建白。

translations.literal: yet the chief ministers are just examining worthies and advancing clerks, daring to raise no proposal.
translations.idiomatic: yet the chancellors are only grading worthies and promoting clerks, not daring to put forward a plan.

sentences.zh: 欲德不用之應，又可驗矣。

translations.literal: The response of "virtue not employed" can again be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The omen of "virtue not employed" can be confirmed again.

sentences.zh: 今陽驕莫解，蟲孽漸熾，河水妄行。

translations.literal: Now yang arrogance cannot be resolved, insect calamities gradually rage, and river waters run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Now yang flares and will not ease, insect plagues swell, and rivers run riot.

sentences.zh: 循依違之跡，行尋常之政，臣恐不足回靈意、塞至戒。

translations.literal: Following tracks of compliance and defiance, conducting ordinary government—I fear it is not enough to turn the numinous mind or block the utmost warning.
translations.idiomatic: Treading paths of hesitation, carrying on ordinary rule—I fear that will not turn Heaven's mind or seal off the supreme warning.

sentences.zh: 古者，穀不登則虧膳，災屢至則降服，凶年不塗塈。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when grain did not ripen they reduced meals; when disasters came repeatedly they lowered garments; in lean years they did not whitewash walls.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity: when grain failed they cut meals; when disasters piled up they lowered dress; in famine years they did not plaster walls.

sentences.zh: 願下詔引咎，損太官之膳，避路寢之朝，許士大夫斥諱上聞，譏切時病。

translations.literal: I beg you to issue an edict taking blame, reduce the Grand Steward's meals, avoid morning audience in the Road Chamber, allow scholars and officials to report taboo matters to the throne, and satirize present ills.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you issue an edict of self-blame, cut the Grand Steward's fare, skip audience in the Road Chamber, let scholars and officials speak forbidden truths to the throne, and rebuke the ills of the day.

sentences.zh: 罷不急之役，省無名之斂，勿崇私恩，更進直道，宣德流化，以休息天下。

translations.literal: Stop non-urgent labor, cut unnamed levies, do not exalt private favor, further advance the straight path, proclaim virtue and spread transformation, and give the realm rest.
translations.idiomatic: Halt unneeded works, abolish nameless exactions, grant no private favor, advance the straight Way, proclaim virtue and spread reform, and let the realm rest.

sentences.zh: 至誠動乎上，大惠浹於下，豈有時澤之艱哉！」

translations.literal: When utmost sincerity moves above and great favor soaks below, how could there be hardship in seasonal blessings!"
translations.idiomatic: When utmost sincerity stirs above and great grace reaches below, what hardship could seasonal rain not end!"

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 會修國史，以絳為編修官，史成，遷祠部員外郎、直集賢院。

translations.literal: When the National History was being compiled, Jiang was made editorial compiler; when the history was finished, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Direct Appointment in the Academy of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: While the National History was in progress he was named editorial compiler; when it was complete he became Vice Director of Rites and Direct Appointment in the Academy of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 時濤官西京，且老矣，因請便養，通判河南府。

translations.literal: At the time his father Tao held office in the Western Capital; being old, he requested convenient nurture and was made administrative vice-prefect of the Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao then served in the Western Capital; old and infirm, he asked for a convenient post and was made vice-prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 又論：「唐室麗正、史官之局，並在大明、華清宮內。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The Tang Directorate of Fine Literature and the historiographers' bureau both lay within the Daming and Huaqing palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Under Tang, the Directorate of Fine Literature and the historiographers' office both stood inside the Daming and Huaqing palaces.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝肇修三館，更立秘閣於昇龍門左，親為飛白書額，作贊刻石閣下。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of our dynasty first restored the Three Halls and further established the Secret Pavilion east of the Ascending Dragon Gate; he personally wrote the plaque in flying-white script and composed an encomium carved in stone beneath the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong first rebuilt the Three Halls and set up the Secret Pavilion east of the Ascending Dragon Gate; he wrote the plaque in flying-white script himself and carved his encomium in stone under the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 景德中，圖書寖廣，真宗皇帝益以內帑四庫。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era books gradually multiplied, and Emperor Zhenzong added the inner treasury's Four Repositories.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde the collections grew, and Emperor Zhenzong enlarged them with the inner treasury's Four Repositories.

sentences.zh: 二聖數嘗臨幸，親加勞問，遞宿廣內者，有不時之召。

translations.literal: Both sagely emperors often visited in person, personally offering encouragement and inquiry; those who lodged within the Broad Interior sometimes received summons at irregular hours.
translations.idiomatic: Both emperors often came in person to encourage and question them; scholars lodged in the inner palace were sometimes summoned at odd hours.

sentences.zh: 人人力道術、究藝文，知天子尊禮甚勤，而名臣高位，繇此其選也。

translations.literal: Men all urged the Way and pursued letters, knowing the Son of Heaven honored learning with utmost diligence—and eminent names and high posts were chosen from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars pressed the Way and studied letters, knowing how diligently the Son of Heaven honored learning—and eminent names and high office came from their ranks.

sentences.zh: 往者遭遘延燔，未遑中葺，或引兩省故事，別建外館，直舍卑喧，民櫩叢接。

translations.literal: Formerly, after the prolonged conflagration, there was no time to rebuild the middle halls; some cited the two departments' precedent and built outer lodges instead—straight quarters low and noisy, common eaves clustered close.
translations.idiomatic: After the great fire there was no time to rebuild the middle halls; citing the two departments' precedent, they built outer lodges—quarters cramped and loud, with common houses pressed close.

sentences.zh: 太官衛尉，供擬滋削，虧體傷風，莫茲為甚。

translations.literal: The Grand Steward and the Commandant of the Guard supplied less and less; the ritual body was wounded and custom harmed—nothing worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward and Commandant of the Guard cut supplies ever further—nothing so harmed ritual and custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下未嘗迂翠華、降玉趾，寥寥冊府，不聞輿馬之音，曠有日矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has never bent the green carriage or lowered the jade foot; the book halls stand empty, unheard the sound of carriage and horse—for many days now.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not turned the imperial carriage or set jade foot in the halls; the archives are silent, no sound of horses or wheels—for a long season now.

sentences.zh: 議者以謂慕道不篤於古，待士少損於前。

translations.literal: Critics say reverence for the Way is less deep than in antiquity and treatment of scholars somewhat diminished from before.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say your love of the Way falls short of antiquity and your regard for scholars has slackened from earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 士無延訪之勤，而因循相尚，不自激策，文雅漸弊，竊為聖朝惜之。

translations.literal: Scholars lack the diligence of extended audiences, and instead drift in mutual imitation, not rousing themselves—letters gradually decay; I privately grieve for the sagely court.
translations.idiomatic: Without the old diligence of imperial audiences, scholars drift in routine and fail to stir themselves—letters decline; I grieve for the court in secret.

sentences.zh: 願辟內館，以恢景德之制。」

translations.literal: I beg that the inner lodges be reopened to restore the Jingde system."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the inner lodges be restored to the Jingde arrangement."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 絳雖在外，猶數論事。

translations.literal: Though Jiang was posted outside the capital, he still repeatedly discussed affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Even while serving outside the capital, Jiang still memorialized often.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「近歲不逞之徒，託言數術，以先生、處士自名，禿巾短褐，內結權幸，外走州邑，甚者矯誣詔書，傲忽官吏。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In recent years unruly men have taken cover under numerology, styling themselves Masters or Recluses, with bald caps and short brown dress; within they bind themselves to the powerful, without they run through prefectures and counties—some even forging edicts and treating officials with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Lately restless men hide behind numerology, calling themselves Master or Recluse in bald cap and short coat; they court power within and roam the provinces without—some even forge edicts and scorn officials.

sentences.zh: 請嚴禁止。

translations.literal: I ask that they be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 嘗以墨敕賜封號者，追還之。」

translations.literal: Those who have received titles by ink edict should have them recalled."
translations.idiomatic: Titles granted by ink edict should be revoked."

sentences.zh: 還權開封府判官，言：

translations.literal: He returned to serve as administrative judge of the Kaifeng prefecture and said:
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice-judge of Kaifeng and said:

sentences.zh: 「蝗亙田野，坌人郛郭，跳擲官寺，井匽皆滿。

translations.literal: "Locusts stretch across the fields, swarm the suburbs, leap into government temples, and wells and privies are all full.
translations.idiomatic: "Locusts blanket the countryside, crowd the suburbs, leap into official temples, and wells and latrines overflow.

sentences.zh: 魯三書螟，《穀梁》以為哀公用田賦虐取於民。

translations.literal: Lu's three records of caterpillars—the Guliang Commentary holds that Duke Ai's use of the field tax cruelly took from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Lu recorded caterpillars three times; the Guliang Commentary says Duke Ai's field tax cruelly squeezed the people.

sentences.zh: 朝廷斂弛之法，近於廉平，以臣愚所聞，似吏不甚稱而召其變。

translations.literal: The court's methods of collection and relaxation are lately near to fair and level; in my humble hearing, it seems officials are not quite adequate and thereby summon this change.
translations.idiomatic: The court's tax policy is nearly fair; yet from what I hear, officials seem inadequate—and that may summon this plague.

sentences.zh: 凡今典城牧民，有顓方面之勢：才者掠功取名，以嚴急為術，或辯偽無實，數蒙獎錄；

translations.literal: All who today hold cities and shepherd the people wield the power of a single face: the capable seize merit and chase fame, taking severity as their art, or argue falsely without substance yet are repeatedly rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: Today's magistrates rule like petty warlords: the able grab credit with harsh methods, or win praise with hollow show;

sentences.zh: 愚者期會簿書，畏首與尾。

translations.literal: the dull merely keep to schedules and ledgers, fearing both head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: the dull only chase deadlines in ledgers, afraid at every turn.

sentences.zh: 二者政殊，而同歸於弊。

translations.literal: The two policies differ, yet alike end in harm.
translations.idiomatic: Their styles differ, yet both end in ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫為國在養民，養民在擇吏，吏循則民安，氣和而災息。

translations.literal: To govern a state lies in nurturing the people; to nurture the people lies in choosing officials; when officials follow the Way the people are secure, qi is harmonious and calamities cease.
translations.idiomatic: A state stands on nurturing the people; nurturing the people stands on choosing officials; when officials keep the Way the people rest, qi harmonizes, and disasters fade.

sentences.zh: 願先取大州邑數十百，詔公卿以下，舉任州守者，使得自辟屬縣令長，務求術略，不限資考。

translations.literal: I beg first to take several tens or hundreds of great prefectures and counties and order the public officials below the chief ministers to recommend those fit to serve as prefects, letting them personally appoint county magistrates and chiefs, striving for strategy and method without limit of qualification or examination.
translations.idiomatic: Take several dozen great prefectures, order ministers to recommend prefects, and let each appoint his own county magistrates, seeking talent and plan without regard to seniority or exams.

sentences.zh: 然後寬以約束，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: Then loosen constraint with broad covenant and allow discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: Then bind them with broad covenant and let them act as need requires.

sentences.zh: 期年條上理狀，或徙或留，必有功化風跡，異乎有司以資而任之者焉。

translations.literal: After one year let them submit reports on governance; transfer or retain as fit—there will surely be achievements, transforming influence, and traces unlike those the departments appoint by qualification alone.
translations.idiomatic: After a year have them report results; move or keep them as merit dictates—then achievement and reform will differ from appointing by seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 漢時，詔問京房災異可息之術，房對以考功課吏。

translations.literal: In Han times, an edict asked Jing Fang what art could quell calamitous anomalies; Fang answered with examining merit and grading officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, the emperor asked Jing Fang how to end strange disasters; Fang answered: examine merit and grade officials.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下博訪理官，除煩苛之命；

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty broadly to consult rectifying officials and remove orders that are troublesome and harsh;
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to seek out upright officials, abolish harsh and tangled orders;

sentences.zh: 申敕計臣，損聚斂之役。

translations.literal: charge the revenue officials and reduce levies that gather and constrict.
translations.idiomatic: charge the revenue officers and cut exactions that pile up.

sentences.zh: 勿起大獄，勿用躁人，務靜安，守淵默。

translations.literal: Do not launch great prosecutions, do not employ rash men; seek quiet peace and keep deep silence.
translations.idiomatic: Raise no great prosecutions, use no rash men; seek stillness and keep deep silence.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『大侵之禮，百官備而不制。』

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "The rites of great famine: the hundred offices are complete but do not fabricate."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "In great famine the hundred offices stand ready but do not create anew."

sentences.zh: 言省事也。

translations.literal: That is to say, reduce administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning: cut redundant government.

sentences.zh: 如此而沴氣不弭，嘉休不至，是靈意𧫩讕，而聖言罔惑歟。」

translations.literal: If after this the baleful qi does not abate and fine blessings do not arrive, then is the numinous intent still unrelenting while sagely words go unheard?"
translations.idiomatic: If even so the harm does not fade and blessing does not come, is Heaven's intent still unyielding while Your words go unheeded?"

sentences.zh: 會郭皇后廢，絳陳《詩白華》，引申后、褒姒事以諷，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, Jiang presented the "White Hua" ode of the Book of Poetry, extending the cases of Shen and Baosi to admonish—the words were most cutting.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed, Jiang cited the "White Hua" ode and the tales of Shen and Baosi to admonish the throne in the sharpest terms.

sentences.zh: 徙三司度支判官，再遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrative judge of the Commission for Revenue and again promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice-judge of the Revenue Commission, then Vice Director of War.

sentences.zh: 上言：「邇來用物滋侈，賜予過制，禁中須索，去年計為緡錢四十五萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Lately the use of goods has grown lavish and grants exceed regulation; inner-palace requisitions last year totaled forty-five thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Lately spending has grown lavish and gifts exceed rule; inner-palace demands last year totaled forty-five thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 自今春至四月，已及二十餘萬。

translations.literal: From this spring through the fourth month, the sum already exceeds twenty thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: From this spring through the fourth month, another twenty thousand and more have been spent.

sentences.zh: 比詔裁節費用，而有司移文，但求咸平、景德簿書。

translations.literal: Though an edict lately ordered frugality, the departments send documents seeking only the ledgers of Xianping and Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lately ordered economy, yet offices ask only for Xianping and Jingde account books.

sentences.zh: 簿書不存，則無所措置。

translations.literal: When the ledgers do not exist, there is nowhere to set hand.
translations.idiomatic: When those books are gone, nothing can be done.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂不若推近及遠，遞考歲用而裁節之，不必咸平、景德為準也。」

translations.literal: I hold that it is better to push from the near to the far, examine yearly outlays in succession and cut them, without needing Xianping and Jingde as the standard."
translations.idiomatic: Better to work from the present backward, review each year's spending in turn and trim—without fixing on Xianping and Jingde alone."

sentences.zh: 初，詔罷織密花透背，禁人服用，且云自掖庭始。

translations.literal: At first an edict forbade weaving dense floral gauze with see-through backing and forbade the people to wear it, saying the prohibition would begin in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict first banned weaving dense floral gauze with see-through backing and forbade the people to wear it, saying the inner palace would lead the ban.

sentences.zh: 既而內人賜衣，復取於有司。

translations.literal: Soon after, inner women given clothing again took it from the departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon palace women given garments took them again from the offices.

sentences.zh: 又後苑作製玳瑁器，索龜筒於市。

translations.literal: Again the rear garden made tortoise-shell vessels in imitation and demanded hawksbill from the market.
translations.idiomatic: Again the rear garden made faux tortoise-shell ware and demanded hawksbill from the market.

sentences.zh: 龜筒，禁物也，民間不得有，而索不已。

translations.literal: Hawksbill is a prohibited item the people may not possess, yet the demand did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Hawksbill is forbidden to commoners, yet the demand never stopped.

sentences.zh: 絳皆論罷之。

translations.literal: Jiang argued against and stopped them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang protested and had each practice halted.

sentences.zh: 又言：「號令數變則虧國體，利害偏聽則惑聰明。

translations.literal: He also said: "When orders change repeatedly the state's body is wounded; when benefit and harm are heard one-sidedly, clarity is confused.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Frequent change of orders wounds the state; hearing only one side of gain and loss clouds judgment.

sentences.zh: 請者務欲各行，而守者患於不一。

translations.literal: Petitioners each strive to have their way carried out, while keepers of the law fear inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: Every petitioner wants his way enforced, while keepers of law fear inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 請罷內降，凡詔令皆由中書、樞密，然後施行。」

translations.literal: I ask that inner directives be abolished; let every edict pass through the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission, then be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish inner directives; let every command go through the Secretariat and Military Commission before execution."

sentences.zh: 因進《聖治箴》五篇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented five chapters of Admonitions for Sagely Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented five chapters of Admonitions for Sagely Governance.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去，服除，擢知制誥，判吏部流內銓、太常禮院。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's mourning; when mourning ended he was promoted to Drafting Edicts, and made judge of the Ministry of Personnel's Inner Selection Bureau and of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He left for his father's mourning; when it ended he was made Drafting Edicts and judge of the Personnel Inner Selection Bureau and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吏部擬官，舊視職田有無，不問多寡，以是不均。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Personnel drafted appointments, it formerly looked only to whether an office field existed, not how much—thus the allotment was unfair.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel appointments once looked only to whether an office field existed, not how large—so allotments were unfair.

sentences.zh: 絳為核其實，以多寡為差，其有名而無實者皆不用，人以為便。

translations.literal: Jiang verified the facts and graded by amount; those with a name but no substance were all set aside—the people thought it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang checked the facts and graded by size; empty titles without land were dropped—everyone found it fair.

sentences.zh: 初改判禮院為知禮儀事，自張絳建請。

translations.literal: The first change of "Judge of the Rites Court" to "Director of Ritual Affairs" began with Zhang Jiang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The change from Judge of the Rites Court to Director of Ritual Affairs began with Zhang Jiang's petition.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還，請知鄧州。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan; on return he requested to know Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to the Khitan he asked to govern Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 距州百二十里，有美陽堰，引湍水溉公田。

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li from the prefecture stood the Meiyang weir, which drew turbulent water to irrigate public fields.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred twenty li from the city stood Meiyang Weir, channeling swift water to irrigate public fields.

sentences.zh: 水來遠而少，利不及民；

translations.literal: The water came from far and was little; the benefit did not reach the people;
translations.idiomatic: The source was distant and the flow slight; the people gained little;

sentences.zh: 濱堰築新土為防，俗謂之墩者，大小又十數，歲數壞，輒調民增築。

translations.literal: Along the weir new earthen dikes called dun were built in another dozen or so sizes; each year several broke, and the people were levied again to rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: Along the bank a dozen earthen dikes called dun were raised; they broke yearly and the people were levied to rebuild.

sentences.zh: 姦人蓄薪茭，以時其急，往往盜決堰墩，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Wicked men stored fuel and rushes and timed the emergency, often stealing to breach weir and dike—the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rascals hoarded reed and brush, timed the crisis, and often breached weir and dike by night—the people groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 絳按召信臣六門堰故跡，距城三里，壅水注鉗廬陂，溉田至三萬頃。

translations.literal: Jiang investigated the old traces of Shao Xinchen's Six Gates Weir, three li from the city; he dammed water to pour into Qianlu Pond and irrigated fields up to thirty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang traced Shao Xinchen's Six Gates Weir three li from the city, dammed the flow into Qianlu Pond, and could irrigate thirty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 請復修之，可罷州人歲役，以水與民，未就而卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He asked to restore it, which could end the prefecture's yearly corvée and give the water to the people; before the work was finished he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to rebuild it, ending yearly corvée and giving the water to the people; he died before it was done, at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 絳以文學知名一時，為人修潔醞藉，所至大興學舍，嘗請諸郡立學。

translations.literal: Jiang was famed in his time for letters; as a man he was refined, cultivated, and restrained; wherever he went he greatly raised schoolhouses, and once asked that every prefecture establish a school.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was renowned for literature, refined and self-possessed; everywhere he went he built schools, and once asked that every commandery found one.

sentences.zh: 在河南修國子學，教諸生，自遠而至者數百人。

translations.literal: In Henan he restored the Imperial University and taught students; several hundred came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan he rebuilt the Imperial University and taught students; several hundred came from distant places.

sentences.zh: 好施宗族，喜賓客，以故，卒之日，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: He was generous to his clan and fond of guests; therefore at his death the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He gave freely to kinsmen and loved to host guests; when he died his house held no spare wealth.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 子景初、景溫、景平、景回。

translations.literal: His sons were Jingchu, Jingwen, Jingping, and Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jingchu, Jingwen, Jingping, and Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 景平好學，著詩書傳說數十篇，終秘書丞。

translations.literal: Jingping loved learning, composed several tens of treatises on the Odes, Documents, and traditions, and ended as Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Jingping was devoted to study, wrote several dozen essays on the Odes, Documents, and classical lore, and died as Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 景回早卒。

translations.literal: Jinghui died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghui died in his youth.

sentences.zh: 子 景溫

translations.literal: Son: Jingwen
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jingwen

sentences.zh: 景溫，字師直。

translations.literal: Jingwen, style name Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, whose courtesy name was Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，通判汝、莫二州，江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as vice-prefect of Ru and Mo prefectures, and as Transport Commission judge for Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was vice-prefect of Ru and Mo, and served as Jiangdong transport commission judge.

sentences.zh: 興宣城百丈圩，議者以為罪，降通判、知漣水軍。

translations.literal: He built the Xuancheng Baizhang polder; critics deemed it a fault; he was demoted to vice-prefect and made military prefect of Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Baizhang polder at Xuancheng; critics called it misconduct, and he was demoted to vice-prefect and made prefect of the Lianshui garrison.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，知諫院邵亢直其前事，徙真州，提點江西刑獄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenzong's reign, Remonstrance Bureau director Shao Kang vindicated his earlier affair; he was transferred to Zhenzhou and made judicial intendant for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, Shao Kang of the Remonstrance Bureau cleared his earlier case; he was moved to Zhenzhou and made Jiangxi judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 歷京西、淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: He served successively as transport commissioner for Jingxi and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner for Jingxi and then Huainan.

sentences.zh: 景溫平生未嘗仕中朝，王安石與之善，又景溫妹嫁其弟安禮，乃驟擢為侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Jingwen had never served at the central court; Wang Anshi was on good terms with him, and Jingwen's sister had married his younger brother Anli; therefore he was suddenly promoted to Attendant Censor with concurrent miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen had never held office in the capital. Wang Anshi favored him, and Jingwen's sister had married Anshi's younger brother Anli, so he was suddenly made Attendant Censor with concurrent miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 安石方惡蘇軾，景溫劾軾向丁憂歸蜀，乘舟商販。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was then hostile to Su Shi; Jingwen impeached Shi for returning to Shu during mourning for his father and trading by boat.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Anshi hostile to Su Shi, Jingwen impeached him for going to Shu during his father's mourning and trading from his boat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷下六路捕逮篙工、水師窮其事，訖無一實。

translations.literal: The court sent orders through the six circuits to seize boatmen and pilots and thoroughly investigate; in the end nothing was substantiated.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the six circuits to seize boatmen and pilots and pursue the case to the end, but nothing was proved.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌等論李定不持母服，景溫察安石指，為辨於前。

translations.literal: Su Song and others argued that Li Ding had not observed mourning for his mother; Jingwen discerned Wang Anshi's intent and pleaded his case before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Song and others argued that Li Ding had not worn mourning for his mother, Jingwen read Wang Anshi's intent and defended him at court.

sentences.zh: 已而事下臺，景溫難違眾議，始云定當追服。

translations.literal: Later the matter went to the Censorate; Jingwen could not defy public opinion and at last said Ding ought to resume mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the Censorate, Jingwen could not defy the consensus and finally said Ding should resume mourning.

sentences.zh: 又言薛向不當得侍從，王韶邊奏誣罔，寖失安石意，然猶以嘗助己，但改直史館兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He also said Xue Xiang ought not receive an inner-court post and that Wang Shao's frontier memorials were deceptive; he gradually lost Wang Anshi's favor, yet because he had once aided him was only changed to Direct Historiographer with concurrent Imperial Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Xue Xiang should not enter the inner court and that Wang Shao's frontier reports were false. He slowly lost Anshi's favor, but because he had once helped him was merely made Direct Historiographer with concurrent Imperial Reader.

sentences.zh: 不敢拜，出知鄧州。

translations.literal: He dared not accept the appointment and went out to govern Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He declined to accept and was sent out to govern Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進陝西都轉運使，以不奉司農約束，改知鄧、襄、澶三州，加直龍圖閣，判將作監。

translations.literal: A year later he was advanced to Grand Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi; for failing to obey the Agriculture Commissioner's rules he was changed to govern Deng, Xiang, and Chan prefectures, given Direct Dragon Diagram Hall, and made judge of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became Shaanxi grand transport commissioner; for not obeying the Agriculture Commissioner's orders he was reassigned to govern Deng, Xiang, and Chan, given Direct Dragon Diagram Hall, and made judge of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 轉右諫議大夫、知潭州。

translations.literal: He became Right Remonstrance Grandee and governor of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and governor of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 章惇開五溪，景溫協力拓築，論功進官，召拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun opened the Five Streams region, Jingwen helped expand the works; for merit he was promoted and summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun opened the Five Streams, Jingwen helped extend the works; for merit he was promoted and summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 復出知洪州、應天府、瀛州。

translations.literal: Again sent out to govern Hongzhou, Yingtian Prefecture, and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out to govern Hongzhou, Yingtian, and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，進寶文閣直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was advanced to Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanyou he was made Baowen Pavilion academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，御史中丞劉摯言其非撥煩吏。

translations.literal: Before a year was out, Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi said he was not skilled at dispatching troublesome clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year was out, Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhi said he was not the man to handle vexing clerks.

sentences.zh: 右司諫王覿言：「瀛州妖婦李自稱事九仙聖母，能與人通語言，談禍福。

translations.literal: Right Bureau Remonstrator Wang Di said: "At Yingzhou a sorceress Li claimed to serve the Nine Immortals' Holy Mother, could converse with people, and speak of fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Right Bureau Remonstrator Wang Di said: "At Yingzhou a sorceress surnamed Li claimed to serve the Nine Immortals' Holy Mother, could speak with people, and foretell fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 景溫在郡為所惑，禮餉甚厚，遣十兵挈之入京。

translations.literal: Jingwen in the prefecture was bewitched by her, honored and fed her lavishly, and sent ten soldiers to escort her to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen in the prefecture was taken in by her, honored and fed her lavishly, and sent ten soldiers to bring her to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數遣子慥至其處；

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent his son Zao to her place;
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent his son Zao to her;

sentences.zh: 補李婿為小史，使出入官府，崇大聲勢；

translations.literal: he appointed Li's son-in-law as a minor clerk, allowing him to come and go in the government offices and swell their prestige;
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Li's son-in-law as a minor clerk, let him pass in and out of the offices, and magnified their prestige;

sentences.zh: 至縱嬖妾之弟，醉歐市人。

translations.literal: he even indulged his favorite concubine's brother, who when drunk beat townspeople in the market.
translations.idiomatic: he even indulged his favorite concubine's brother, who when drunk beat people in the market.

sentences.zh: 為政若此，尚何惜而不加譴。」

translations.literal: To govern thus, how could one spare him from censure?"
translations.idiomatic: With government like this, how could he escape censure?"

sentences.zh: 於是罷知蔡州。

translations.literal: Therefore he was removed to govern Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore removed to govern Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年初，置權六曹尚書，以為刑部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, provisional Six Ministries Directors were established; he was made Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the third year provisional directors of the Six Ministries were created; he was made Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 劉安世復論之，改知鄆州，再歷永興軍。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi again criticized him; he was changed to govern Yanzhou and later served again at Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi criticized him again; he was moved to Yanzhou and later served again at Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 時章惇為相，景溫言元祐大臣改先帝之政，並西夏人偃蹇終未順命，宜罷分畫，以馬跡所至為境。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun was chief councilor, Jingwen said the Yuanyou grandees had altered the late emperor's policies and the Western Xia remained recalcitrant and had never submitted; the partitioned borders ought to be abolished and the frontier fixed wherever horse hooves could reach.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Dun as chief councilor, Jingwen said the Yuanyou ministers had overturned the late emperor's policies and the Western Xia remained defiant and unsubmissive; the partitioned borders should be abolished and the frontier drawn wherever horses could go.

sentences.zh: 惇用其說，徙知河陽，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun adopted his view; he was transferred to govern Heyang, died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun took his advice; he was transferred to Heyang, died, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 葉清臣

translations.literal: Ye Qingchen
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qingchen

sentences.zh: 葉清臣，字道卿，蘇州長洲人。

translations.literal: Ye Qingchen, style name Daoqing, was a native of Changzhou in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qingchen, whose courtesy name was Daoqing, came from Changzhou in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父參，終光祿卿。

translations.literal: His father Can ended as Director of Palace Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: His father Can rose to Director of Palace Banquets.

sentences.zh: 清臣幼敏異，好學善屬文。

translations.literal: Qingchen was clever and unusual as a child, loved learning, and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was precocious as a boy, loved learning, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年，舉進士，知舉劉筠奇所對策，擢第二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng he passed the jinshi examination; the chief examiner Liu Yun marveled at his policy essay and ranked him second.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiansheng he passed the jinshi; chief examiner Liu Yun was struck by his policy essay and ranked him second.

sentences.zh: 宋進士以策擢高第，自清臣始。

translations.literal: For Song jinshi to be advanced to high rank by the policy essay began with Qingchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Song practice of promoting jinshi to high rank on the strength of the policy essay began with Qingchen.

sentences.zh: 授太常寺奉禮郎、簽書蘇州觀察判官事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Ceremonial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and signing secretary for the Suzhou Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Ceremonial Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and signing secretary on the Suzhou observation staff.

sentences.zh: 還為光祿寺丞、集賢校理，通判太平州、知秀州。

translations.literal: He returned as Assistant Director of Palace Banquets and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, vice-prefect of Taiping, and prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as assistant director of palace banquets and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was vice-prefect of Taiping, and governed Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入判三司戶部勾院，改鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He entered as judge of the Finance Commission's Personnel Reconciliation Bureau and was changed to Salt and Iron judge.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as judge of the Finance Commission personnel reconciliation bureau and became Salt and Iron judge.

sentences.zh: 上言九事：請遣使循行天下，知民疾苦，察吏能否；

translations.literal: He memorialized nine proposals: send envoys to tour the realm to learn the people's hardships and test officials' ability;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized nine proposals: send envoys to tour the empire, learn the people's hardships, and judge officials' competence;

sentences.zh: 興太學，選置博士，許公卿大臣子弟補學生；

translations.literal: expand the Imperial University, select and appoint erudites, and allow sons of dukes, ministers, and great officials to enter as students;
translations.idiomatic: expand the Imperial University, appoint erudites, and let sons of dukes, ministers, and high officials enroll as students;

sentences.zh: 重縣令；

translations.literal: give weight to county magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: raise the standing of county magistrates;

sentences.zh: 諸科舉人取名大義，責以策問；

translations.literal: for the various examination categories, take names with broad meaning and examine them by policy questions;
translations.idiomatic: for the various examination tracks, choose candidates for broad learning and test them with policy questions;

sentences.zh: 省流外官，無得入仕；

translations.literal: reduce outer-service officials and forbid them from entering office;
translations.idiomatic: cut outer-service officials and bar them from office;

sentences.zh: 聽武臣終三年之喪；

translations.literal: allow military officials to complete the three-year mourning;
translations.idiomatic: let military officers observe the full three-year mourning;

sentences.zh: 罷度僧；

translations.literal: abolish ordaining monks;
translations.idiomatic: end the ordination of monks;

sentences.zh: 廢讀經一業；

translations.literal: abolish the single study of scripture recitation;
translations.idiomatic: abolish the scripture-recitation track alone;

sentences.zh: 訓兵練將，慎出令，簡條約。

translations.literal: train soldiers and drill generals, be cautious in issuing orders, and simplify regulations.
translations.idiomatic: drill troops and train generals, issue orders cautiously, and simplify rules.

sentences.zh: 詞多不載。

translations.literal: Most of the wording is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 出知宣州，累遷太常丞，同修起居注，判三司鹽鐵勾院，進直史館。

translations.literal: He went out to govern Xuanzhou, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, co-compiled the Veritable Records, judged the Salt and Iron Reconciliation Bureau, and advanced to Direct Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to Xuanzhou, he rose to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, helped compile the Veritable Records, judged the salt and iron reconciliation bureau, and was made Direct Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 是冬，京師地震，上疏曰：「天以陽動，君之道也；

translations.literal: That winter the capital was shaken by earthquake; he submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven moves by yang—the way of the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital was shaken by an earthquake. He memorialized: "Heaven moves through yang—the way of the ruler;

sentences.zh: 地以陰靜，臣之道也。

translations.literal: earth rests in yin—the way of the minister.
translations.idiomatic: earth rests in yin—the way of the minister.

sentences.zh: 天動地靜，主尊臣卑。

translations.literal: Heaven moves and earth is still: the lord is exalted, the minister is low.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven moves, earth is still: the sovereign is high, the minister is low.

sentences.zh: 易此則亂，地為之震。

translations.literal: To reverse this is disorder, and the earth quakes for it.
translations.idiomatic: Reverse this and there is chaos, and the earth quakes.

sentences.zh: 乃十二月二日丙夜，京師地震，移刻而止；

translations.literal: On the second day of the twelfth month, at the hour of bing by night, the capital quaked and stopped after a moment;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the second day of the twelfth month, at the hour of bing, the capital shook and stopped after a time;

sentences.zh: 定襄同日震，至五日不止，壞廬寺，殺人畜，凡十之六。

translations.literal: Dingxiang quaked the same day and did not stop until the fifth day, destroying houses and temples and killing people and livestock—six tenths of all.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang shook the same day and did not stop until the fifth, destroying houses and temples and killing people and livestock—six in ten.

sentences.zh: 大河之東，彌千五百里而及都下，誠大異也。

translations.literal: East of the Great River, for more than fifteen hundred li up to the capital—truly a great anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yellow River, for fifteen hundred li to the capital—it was a great portent indeed.

sentences.zh: 屬者熒惑犯南斗，治曆者相顧而駭。

translations.literal: Recently Mars had trespassed on the Southern Dipper, and calendar-makers looked at one another in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Mars had lately encroached on the Southern Dipper, and the calendar-makers were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 陛下憂勤庶政，方夏泰寧，而一歲之中，災變仍見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is diligent in government and the realm was at peace in summer, yet within a year calamities have recurred.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty labors over government and the realm was tranquil in summer, yet within a year omens have recurred.

sentences.zh: 必有下失民望、上戾天意者，故垂戒以啟迪清衷。

translations.literal: There must be failure below that loses the people's hope and offense above that angers Heaven's mind; therefore warnings are sent to awaken a pure heart.
translations.idiomatic: Something below must have lost the people's trust and something above must have offended Heaven; these warnings come to awaken a pure heart.

sentences.zh: 而陛下泰然不以為異，徒使內侍走四方，治佛事，修道科，非所謂消復之實也。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty is calm and does not regard them as strange, only sending inner attendants about the realm to manage Buddhist affairs and Daoist rites—not what is called real restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty is calm and treats them as nothing strange, only sending palace attendants about the realm for Buddhist rites and Daoist observances—not true restoration.

sentences.zh: 頃范仲淹、余靖以言事被黜，天下之人，齰舌不敢議朝政者，行將二年。

translations.literal: Not long ago Fan Zhongyan and Yu Jing were dismissed for remonstrance; for nearly two years men under heaven have clenched their tongues and dared not discuss court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Fan Zhongyan and Yu Jing were dismissed for speaking out; for nearly two years the empire has held its tongue and dared not discuss court policy.

sentences.zh: 願陛下深自咎責，許延忠直敢言之士，庶幾明威降鑒，而善應來集也。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to blame yourself deeply and allow loyal, outspoken men to be retained; then perhaps bright authority will descend and good responses gather."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to blame yourself deeply and welcome loyal men who dare speak plainly; then perhaps Heaven will look down and good omens will gather."

sentences.zh: 書奏數日，仲淹等皆得近徙。

translations.literal: Several days after the memorial was submitted, Zhongyan and the others were all moved nearer the court.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of the memorial, Zhongyan and the others were all brought closer to court.

sentences.zh: 會詔求直言，清臣復上疏言大臣專政，仁宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the court called for blunt speech, Qingchen again memorialized on great ministers' monopoly of power; Renzong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought blunt speech, Qingchen again memorialized that great ministers monopolized power; Renzong praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 清臣請外，為兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: Qingchen asked to leave the capital and became deputy transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen asked to leave the capital and became deputy transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 並太湖有民田，豪右據上遊，水不得泄，而民不敢訴。

translations.literal: Along Taihu were commoners' fields; powerful families held the upper reaches so water could not drain, and the people dared not sue.
translations.idiomatic: Along Taihu were commoners' fields; powerful families held the upper reaches so water could not drain, and the people dared not complain.

sentences.zh: 嘗建請疏盤龍彙、滬瀆港入於海，民賴其利。

translations.literal: He once petitioned to open Panlong Creek and the Hudu harbor to the sea, and the people profited.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to channel Panlong Creek and Hudu Harbor to the sea, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 以右正言知制誥，知審官院，判國子監。

translations.literal: He became Right Remonstrator Drafting Edicts, director of the Bureau of Review, and judge of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrator drafting edicts, director of the Bureau of Review, and judge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時陝西用兵，上言：「當今將不素蓄，兵不素練，財無久積。

translations.literal: At the time Shaanxi was at war; he said: "Today generals are not long trained, soldiers not long drilled, and funds not long stored.
translations.idiomatic: With war on the Shaanxi frontier he said: "Today generals are not long trained, soldiers not long drilled, and funds not long stored.

sentences.zh: 小有邊警，外無驍將，內無重兵。

translations.literal: At a small frontier alarm there are no fierce generals without and no heavy troops within.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest frontier alarm there are no fierce generals outside and no heavy troops within.

sentences.zh: 舉西北二垂觀之，若落大瓠，外示雄壯，其中空洞，了無一物。

translations.literal: Look at the northwestern two frontiers: it is like a great gourd fallen—outwardly it seems bold and strong, yet within it is hollow and holds nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Look at the northwestern frontiers: it is like a great gourd—outwardly bold, inwardly hollow, holding nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 脫不幸戎馬猖突，腹內諸城，非可以計術守也。

translations.literal: If by misfortune barbarian horses should burst forth, the inner prefectures cannot be held by stratagem alone.
translations.idiomatic: If barbarian horses should burst forth, the inner prefectures cannot be held by stratagem alone.

sentences.zh: 自元昊僭竊，因循至於延州之寇，中間一歲矣。

translations.literal: Since Yuanhao's usurpation, delay has continued to the raid on Yanzhou—a full year between.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanhao's rebellion, delay has continued to the Yanzhou raid—a full year has passed.

sentences.zh: 而屯戍無術，資糧不充，窮年畜兵，了不足用，連監牧馬，未幾已虛。

translations.literal: Yet garrison methods are wanting, provisions insufficient; troops are kept a full year yet are barely usable; even the border pasture horses are soon exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet garrison methods fail, provisions run short; troops are kept a year yet are barely usable; even the border pasture horses are soon spent.

sentences.zh: 使蚩蚩之無所倚而安者，此臣所以孜孜憂大瓠之穿也。

translations.literal: To leave the people with nothing to lean on in peace—this is why I fret that the great gourd will be pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: To leave the people nothing to lean on in peace—this is why I fret that the great gourd will be pierced through.

sentences.zh: 今羌戎稍卻，變詐亡窮，豈宜乘即時之小安，忘前日之大辱？

translations.literal: Now the Qiang and Rong have slightly withdrawn, yet their shifts and deceits are endless; how can one take this moment's small peace and forget yesterday's great humiliation?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Qiang and Rong have slightly withdrawn, yet their shifts and deceits never end; how can one take this small peace and forget yesterday's great humiliation?

sentences.zh: 又將泰然自處，則後日視今，猶今之視前也。」

translations.literal: If the generals settle into complacency again, then the day to come will look on today as today looks on yesterday."
translations.idiomatic: If the generals settle into complacency again, then the future will look on today as today looks on yesterday."

sentences.zh: 元昊圍延州，既解去，鈐轄內侍盧守懃與通判計用章更訟於朝。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao besieged Yanzhou and then withdrew, Military Commission eunuch Lu Shouqin and vice-prefect Ji Yongzhang renewed their lawsuits at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao besieged Yanzhou and withdrew, eunuch Military Commission controller Lu Shouqin and vice-prefect Ji Yongzhang renewed their lawsuits at court.

sentences.zh: 時內侍用事者，多為守懃遊說，朝廷議薄守懃罪，而流用章嶺南。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in power at the time mostly lobbied for Shouqin; the court debated lightening Shouqin's guilt while exiling Yongzhang to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful eunuchs mostly lobbied for Shouqin; the court debated lightening his guilt while exiling Yongzhang to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 清臣上疏曰：「臣聞眾議，延州之圍，盧守懃首對范雍號泣，謀遣李康伯見元昊，為偷生之計。

translations.literal: Qingchen submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard public discussion: in the siege of Yanzhou, Lu Shouqin was the first to face Fan Yong in tears and planned to send Li Kangbo to see Yuanhao—a plan to save his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen memorialized: "I hear it said that in the Yanzhou siege Lu Shouqin was first to face Fan Yong in tears and planned to send Li Kangbo to Yuanhao—a plan to save his own skin.

sentences.zh: 計用章以為事急，不若退保鄜州，李康伯遂有『死難，不可出城見賊』之語。

translations.literal: Ji Yongzhang held that the matter was urgent and it was better to withdraw and hold Fuzhou; Li Kangbo then had the words, "Better die than leave the city to see the bandits."
