translations.idiomatic: Ji Yongzhang said the crisis was urgent and it was better to fall back on Fuzhou; Li Kangbo then said, "Better die than leave the city to see the enemy."

sentences.zh: 自元昊退，守懃懼金明之失、二將之沒，朝廷歸罪邊將；

translations.literal: After Yuanhao withdrew, Shouqin feared blame for the loss at Jinming and the death of the two generals; the court would blame the frontier commanders;
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhao withdrew, Shouqin feared blame for the Jinming loss and the two generals' deaths; the court would blame the frontier commanders;

sentences.zh: 又思倉卒之言，一旦為人所發，則禍在不測。

translations.literal: he also feared that hasty words might one day be exposed by others, and disaster would be unforeseeable.
translations.idiomatic: he also feared that rash words might one day be exposed, with unforeseeable consequences.

sentences.zh: 遂反覆前議，移過於人，先為奏陳，冀望取信。

translations.literal: He therefore reversed his earlier position, shifted blame onto others, memorialized first, and hoped to win credence.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed his earlier stance, shifted blame onto others, memorialized first, and hoped to be believed.

sentences.zh: 正如黃德和誣奏劉平，欲免退走之罪。

translations.literal: It is just as when Huang Dehe falsely impeached Liu Ping to escape the crime of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: This is like Huang Dehe's false impeachment of Liu Ping to escape the crime of flight.

sentences.zh: 尋聞計用章亦疏斥守懃事狀，詔文彥博置劾，未分曲直，而遽罪用章、康伯，特赦守懃。

translations.literal: Soon it was heard that Ji Yongzhang also memorialized against Shouqin; an edict ordered Wen Yanbo to investigate, yet before right and wrong were settled Yongzhang and Kangbo were suddenly punished while Shouqin was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ji Yongzhang too memorialized against Shouqin; Wen Yanbo was ordered to investigate, yet before guilt was settled Yongzhang and Kangbo were punished while Shouqin was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 此必有議者結中人、惑聖聽，以為方當用師邊陲，不可輕起大獄。

translations.literal: There must be critics who linked with inner attendants and confused the imperial ear, thinking that with troops on the frontier one must not lightly raise a great case.
translations.idiomatic: Someone must have colluded with palace attendants and confused the throne, arguing that with troops on the frontier one must not lightly raise a major case.

sentences.zh: 臣觀前史，魏尚、陳湯雖有功，尚不免削爵，罰作案驗吏士。

translations.literal: I observe former histories: Wei Shang and Chen Tang, though they had merit, still could not avoid losing rank and being punished as investigating officers.
translations.idiomatic: In former histories Wei Shang and Chen Tang, though meritorious, still lost rank and were punished as investigating officers.

sentences.zh: 何況擁兵自固，觀望不出，恣縱羌賊，破一縣，擒二將。

translations.literal: How much more when one holds troops and fortifies himself, watches and does not advance, indulges Qiang bandits, destroys a county, and captures two generals.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one holds troops, fortifies himself, watches without advancing, indulges Qiang raiders, destroys a county, and captures two generals.

sentences.zh: 大罪未戮，又自蔽其過，矯誣上奏，此而不按，何罪不容？

translations.literal: The great crime is not punished, yet he covers his own fault and falsely impeaches in memorial—if this is not prosecuted, what crime would not be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: A great crime goes unpunished while he hides his fault and falsely impeaches—if this is not prosecuted, what crime would not be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 設用章有退保之言，止坐畏懦；

translations.literal: Suppose Yongzhang had words about withdrawing to hold the city—he would bear only the charge of cowardice;
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yongzhang had spoken of withdrawing to hold the city, that is only cowardice;

sentences.zh: 而守懃謀見賊之行，乃是歸款。

translations.literal: but Shouqin's plan to go out and see the bandits was surrender.
translations.idiomatic: but Shouqin's plan to go out and see the enemy was surrender.

sentences.zh: 二者之責，孰重孰輕，望詔彥博鞫正其獄。

translations.literal: Between the two charges, which is heavy and which light—I beg that Yanbo be ordered to judge the case correctly.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two, which charge is heavier—I beg that Yanbo be ordered to judge the case correctly.

sentences.zh: 苟用章之狀果虛，守懃之罪果白，用章更置重科，物論亦允。

translations.literal: If Yongzhang's account proves false and Shouqin's guilt proves clear, let Yongzhang receive the heavier sentence and public opinion will be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: If Yongzhang's account proves false and Shouqin's guilt is clear, let Yongzhang receive the heavier sentence and opinion will be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 無容偏聽一辭，以虧王道無黨之義。」

translations.literal: Do not heed one side alone and wound the kingly way of impartiality."
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed one side alone and wound the kingly way of impartiality."

sentences.zh: 其後獄具，守懃才降湖北兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Afterward the case was concluded, and only then was Shouqin demoted to Supervisory Commissioner of Hubei Troops and Horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, Shouqin was demoted only to Supervisory Commissioner of Hubei Troops and Horses.

sentences.zh: 時西師未解，急於經費，中書進擬三司使，清臣初不在選中。

translations.literal: At the time the western campaign had not ended and funds were urgently needed; the Secretariat advanced nominees for Finance Commissioner, and Qingchen was not initially among those chosen.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign was still unresolved and funds were urgently needed; the Secretariat proposed nominees for finance commissioner, and Qingchen was not initially on the list.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「葉清臣才可用。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Ye Qingchen's talent can be put to use."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Ye Qingchen's talent can be put to use."

sentences.zh: 擢為起居舍人、龍圖閣學士、權三司使公事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist, Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and Acting Commissioner for Finance Commission Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to diarist, Dragon Diagram Hall academician, and acting commissioner for finance commission affairs.

sentences.zh: 始奏編前後詔敕，使吏不能欺，簿帳之叢冗者，一切刪去。

translations.literal: He first memorialized to compile edicts issued before and after, so that clerks could not deceive; all redundant account books were deleted.
translations.idiomatic: He first had edicts past and present compiled into registers so clerks could not deceive, and cut away every redundant ledger.

sentences.zh: 內東門、御廚皆內侍領之，凡所呼索，有司不敢問，乃為合同以檢其出入。

translations.literal: The Inner East Gate and the Imperial Kitchen were both run by inner attendants; whatever they called for, the responsible offices did not dare question it, so he drew up joint agreements to inspect what went in and out.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner East Gate and Imperial Kitchen were both run by palace eunuchs; whatever they requisitioned, regular offices did not dare ask, so he drew up joint agreements to audit their comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 清臣與宋庠、鄭戩雅相善，為呂夷簡所惡，出知江寧府。

translations.literal: Qingchen was on close terms with Song Kuan and Zheng Yan, but was hated by Lü Yijian and was sent out as prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was close to Song Kuan and Zheng Yan but was disliked by Lü Yijian and was sent out to govern Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 逾年，入翰林學士，知通進銀臺司、勾當三班院。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered the Hanlin Academy as academician, took charge of the Communications Silver Terrace Office, and managed the Three-Class Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he entered the Hanlin as academician, supervised the Communications Silver Terrace Office, and managed the Three-Class Bureau.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，言者以清臣為知兵，請起守邊。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning; memorializers said Qingchen understood military affairs and asked that he be recalled to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he entered mourning; critics said Qingchen knew military affairs and asked that he be recalled to the border.

sentences.zh: 及服除，宰相陳執中素不悅之，即除翰林侍讀學士、知邠州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Chancellor Chen Zhizhong, who had never liked him, immediately appointed him Hanlin Reader and prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Chancellor Chen Zhizhong, who had never favored him, immediately made him Hanlin Reader and prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 道由京師，因請對，改澶州，進尚書戶部郎中、知青州。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital on his way, he requested an audience, was reassigned to Chan, and was advanced to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital en route, he requested an audience, was moved to Chan, and was advanced to director in the Revenue Ministry and prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 徙知永興軍，浚三白渠，溉田逾六千頃。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yongxing Circuit, dredged the Sanbai Canal, and irrigated more than six thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yongxing Circuit, dredged the Sanbai Canal, and irrigated more than six thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 仁宗御天章閣，召公卿，出手詔問當世急務。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong attended at the Tianzhang Pavilion, summoned the chief ministers, and handed down an edict in his own hand asking about the urgent affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong attended at the Tianzhang Pavilion, summoned chief ministers, and handed down a personal edict asking about the urgent affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 清臣聞之，為條對，極論時政闕失，其言多劘切權貴。

translations.literal: When Qingchen heard of it he drew up an itemized reply, discussing at length the failures of current policy; his words were largely sharp against the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Qingchen drew up an itemized reply and spoke at length on the failures of current policy, much of it sharply cutting at the powerful.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「陛下欲息奔競，此係中書。

translations.literal: He also said, "If Your Majesty wishes to still frantic competition, this depends on the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "If Your Majesty wishes to still frantic competition, this depends on the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 若宰相裁抑奔競之流，則風俗惇厚，人知止足；

translations.literal: If the chancellor restrains those who rush to compete, custom will grow sincere and people will know when to stop;
translations.idiomatic: If the chancellor restrains the frantic, custom will grow sincere and people will know contentment;

sentences.zh: 宰相用憸佞之士，則貪榮冒進，激成渾波。

translations.literal: but if the chancellor employs fawning and treacherous men, they will greed for glory and rush ahead, stirring up muddy waves.
translations.idiomatic: but if the chancellor employs fawning and treacherous men, they will greed for glory and rush ahead and stir muddy waves.

sentences.zh: 向有職在管庫，日趨走時相之門。

translations.literal: Formerly there were officials in charge of storehouses who daily hurried to the current chancellor's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly officials in charge of storehouses daily hurried to the current chancellor's gate.

sentences.zh: 入則取街談巷言，以資耳目；

translations.literal: Going in they gathered street talk and alley gossip to inform his ears and eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Going in they gathered street talk and alley gossip to inform his ears and eyes;

sentences.zh: 出則竊廟謨朝論，以驚流輩。

translations.literal: going out they stole court counsels and court debates to startle their peers.
translations.idiomatic: going out they stole court counsels and court debates to startle their peers.

sentences.zh: 一旦皆擢職司，以酬所任。

translations.literal: In a single day they were all promoted to offices to repay what they had done.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day they were all promoted to offices to repay their service.

sentences.zh: 比日人士競踵此風，出入權要之家，時有『三屍』、『五鬼』之號。

translations.literal: Recently people have competed to follow this fashion, going in and out of the houses of men in power, and were sometimes called the "Three Corpses" and the "Five Ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: Lately men have competed to follow this fashion, passing in and out of the houses of the powerful, and were sometimes called the "Three Corpses" and the "Five Ghosts."

sentences.zh: 乃列館職，或置省曹。

translations.literal: They were then listed in Hanlin posts or placed in ministry bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: They were then given Hanlin posts or placed in ministry bureaus.

sentences.zh: 且臺諫官為天子耳目，今則不然，盡為宰相肘腋。

translations.literal: Moreover, remonstrance and censorial officials are the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; now it is not so—they have all become the chancellor's henchmen.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and censorial officials should be the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; now they are not—all have become the chancellor's henchmen.

sentences.zh: 宰相所惡，則捃以微瑕，公行擊搏；

translations.literal: Those the chancellor hates, they gather minor flaws and openly attack;
translations.idiomatic: Those the chancellor hates, they gather minor flaws and attack openly;

sentences.zh: 宰相所善，則從而唱和，為之先容。

translations.literal: those the chancellor favors, they echo him and make introductions for him.
translations.idiomatic: those the chancellor favors, they echo him and pave the way for him.

sentences.zh: 中書政令不平，賞罰不當，則箝口結舌，未嘗敢言。

translations.literal: When Secretariat policies are unfair and rewards and punishments are wrong, they clamp their mouths shut and never dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Secretariat policies are unfair and rewards and punishments are wrong, they clamp their mouths shut and never dare speak.

sentences.zh: 人主纖微過差，或宮闈小事，即極言過當，用為訐直。

translations.literal: For the ruler's minute faults or palace trifles, they speak to excess and use it as frankness.
translations.idiomatic: For the ruler's minute faults or palace trifles, they speak to excess and call it frankness.

sentences.zh: 供職未逾歲時，遷擢已加常等。

translations.literal: Before they have served a year, their promotions already exceed the usual grade.
translations.idiomatic: Before they have served a year, their promotions already exceed the usual grade.

sentences.zh: 宋禧為御史，勸陛下宮中畜犬設棘，以為守衛。

translations.literal: Song Xi, as censor, advised Your Majesty to keep dogs in the palace and set thorn hedges as guards.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xi, as censor, advised Your Majesty to keep dogs in the palace and set thorn hedges for guards.

sentences.zh: 削弱朝體，取笑四夷，不加訶譴，擢為諫官。

translations.literal: This weakens the dignity of the court and makes a laughingstock of the four barbarians, yet without rebuke he was promoted to remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: This weakens court dignity and makes a laughingstock of the four barbarians, yet without rebuke he was promoted to remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 王達兩為湖南、江西轉運使，所至苛虐，誅剝百姓，徒配無辜，特以宰相故舊，不次拔擢，遂有河北之行。

translations.literal: Wang Da twice served as transport commissioner in Hunan and Jiangxi; wherever he went he was harsh and cruel, stripped the people, and exiled the innocent, yet solely because he was an old friend of the chancellor he was promoted out of turn and was then given an appointment in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Da twice served as transport commissioner in Hunan and Jiangxi; wherever he went he was harsh and cruel, stripped the people, and exiled the innocent, yet solely as an old friend of the chancellor he was promoted out of turn and then sent to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 如此，是長奔競也。」

translations.literal: In this way frantic competition is nourished."
translations.idiomatic: That is how frantic competition is nourished."

sentences.zh: 其他所列利害甚眾。

translations.literal: The other harms he listed were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The other harms he listed were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 會河決商胡，北道艱食，復以為翰林學士、權三司使。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke at Shanghu and the northern routes were short of food, he was again made Hanlin academician and acting finance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Shanghu and the northern routes were short of food, he was again made Hanlin academician and acting finance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舊制，有三司使、權使公事，而清臣所除，止言「權使」，自是分三等焉。

translations.literal: Under the old system there were a finance commissioner and an acting commissioner for commission affairs, but Qingchen's appointment spoke only of "acting commissioner," and from then there were three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system there were a finance commissioner and an acting commissioner for commission affairs, but Qingchen's appointment spoke only of "acting commissioner," and from then there were three grades.

sentences.zh: 以戶部副使向傳式不職，奏請出之。

translations.literal: Because the vice commissioner of the Household Bureau, Xiang Chuanshi, was negligent in duty, he memorialized to have him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Household Bureau vice commissioner Xiang Chuanshi was negligent, he memorialized to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年春，帝御便殿，訪近臣以備邊之策。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Huangyou the Emperor attended at the side hall and asked close ministers for policies to prepare the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Huangyou the Emperor attended at the side hall and asked close ministers for policies to prepare the border.

sentences.zh: 清臣上對，略曰：

translations.literal: Qingchen replied in summary, saying in part:
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen replied in summary, saying in part:

sentences.zh: 「陛下臨御天下，二十八年，未嘗一日自暇自逸。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has ruled the realm for twenty-eight years and has never taken a single day of leisure or ease.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has ruled the realm for twenty-eight years and has never taken a single day of leisure or ease.

sentences.zh: 而西夏、契丹頻歲為患者，豈非將相大臣，不得其人，不能為陛下張威德而攘四夷乎？

translations.literal: Yet Xi Xia and the Khitan have troubled us year after year—is it not because generals, ministers, and great officials are not the right men and cannot spread Your Majesty's might and drive off the four barbarians?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xi Xia and the Khitan have troubled us year after year—is it not because generals, ministers, and great officials are not the right men and cannot spread Your Majesty's might and drive off the four barbarians?

sentences.zh: 昔王商在廷，單于不敢仰視；

translations.literal: Formerly when Wang Shang was at court the Chanyu dared not look up;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Wang Shang was at court the Chanyu dared not look up;

sentences.zh: 郅都臨代，匈奴不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: when Zhi Du faced Dai the Xiongnu dared not violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhi Du faced Dai the Xiongnu dared not violate the border.

sentences.zh: 今內則輔相寡謀，綱紀不振；

translations.literal: Now within, assisting ministers lack strategy and discipline is not restored;
translations.idiomatic: Now within, assisting ministers lack strategy and discipline is not restored;

sentences.zh: 外則兵不素練，將不素蓄。

translations.literal: without, troops are not trained in peace and generals are not stored up in advance.
translations.idiomatic: without, troops are not trained in peace and generals are not stored up in advance.

sentences.zh: 此外寇得以內侮也。

translations.literal: Thus outer enemies are able to insult us from within.
translations.idiomatic: Thus outer enemies are able to insult us from within.

sentences.zh: 慶曆，劉六符來，執政無術略，不能折衝樽俎，以破其謀。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era Liu Liufu came; the rulers lacked strategy and could not settle matters at the banquet table to break his plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingli era Liu Liufu came; the rulers lacked strategy and could not settle matters at the banquet table to break his plot.

sentences.zh: 六符初亦疑大國之有人，藏姦計而未發。

translations.literal: At first Liufu also doubted that the great state had capable men and hid his treacherous plan without launching it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liufu also doubted that the great state had capable men and hid his treacherous plan without launching it.

sentences.zh: 既見表裏，遂肆陸梁。

translations.literal: Once he had seen us inside and out, he then rampaged insolently.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had seen us inside and out, he then rampaged insolently.

sentences.zh: 只煩一介之使，坐致二十萬物，永匱膏血，以奉腥膻。

translations.literal: It took only troubling a single envoy to sit and bring about two hundred thousand goods, forever draining the nation's marrow to feed rank stench.
translations.idiomatic: It took only troubling a single envoy to sit and bring about two hundred thousand goods, forever draining the nation's marrow to feed rank stench.

sentences.zh: 此有識之士，所以為國長太息也。

translations.literal: This is why men of discernment sigh long for the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is why men of discernment sigh long for the state.

sentences.zh: 今詔問：「北使詣闕，以伐西戎為名，即有邀求，何以答之？」

translations.literal: Now the edict asks, "A northern envoy comes to court under the pretext of attacking the Western Rong; if he makes demands, how are we to answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict asks, "A northern envoy comes to court under the pretext of attacking the Western Rong; if he makes demands, how are we to answer?"

sentences.zh: 臣聞誓書所載，彼此無求。

translations.literal: I have heard that the covenant records state that neither side seeks from the other.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the covenant records state that neither side seeks from the other.

sentences.zh: 況元昊叛邊，累年致討，契丹坐觀金鼓之出，豈有毫髮之助？

translations.literal: Moreover Yuanhao rebelled on the border and we have campaigned against him for years, while the Khitan sat watching our drums and banners go forth—what hair's breadth of help did they give?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yuanhao rebelled on the border and we have campaigned against him for years, while the Khitan sat watching our drums and banners go forth—what hair's breadth of help did they give?

sentences.zh: 今彼國出師，輒求我助，奸盟違約，不亦甚乎？

translations.literal: Now their state sends troops and immediately asks our aid—is not this a wicked breach of the covenant and extreme indeed?
translations.idiomatic: Now their state sends troops and immediately asks our aid—is not this a wicked breach of the covenant and extreme indeed?

sentences.zh: 若使辯捷之人，判其曲直，要之一戰，以破其謀，我直彼曲，豈不憚服。

translations.literal: If we send an eloquent man to judge right and wrong and insist on one battle to break their plot, we are straight and they are crooked—would they not fear and submit?
translations.idiomatic: If we send an eloquent man to judge right and wrong and insist on one battle to break their plot, we are straight and they are crooked—would they not fear and submit?

sentences.zh: 苟不知咎，或肆侵陵，方河朔災傷之餘，野無廬舍，我堅壁自守，縱令深入，其能久居？

translations.literal: If they do not know their fault and perhaps raid wantonly, the Hebei and Shuo region has just suffered disaster and the fields have no huts; if we hold our walls and defend ourselves, even if we let them advance deep, how long can they stay?
translations.idiomatic: If they do not know their fault and perhaps raid wantonly, the Hebei and Shuo region has just suffered disaster and the fields have no huts; if we hold our walls and defend ourselves, even if we let them advance deep, how long can they stay?

sentences.zh: 既無所因之糧，則亟當遁去。

translations.literal: With no grain to rely on, they should flee at once.
translations.idiomatic: With no grain to rely on, they should flee at once.

sentences.zh: 然後選擇驍勇，遏絕歸師，設伏出奇，邀擊首尾，若不就禽，亦且大敗矣。

translations.literal: Then choose the brave and bold, cut off their returning army, set ambushes and strike with surprise, and attack head and tail; if they are not captured, they will still suffer a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Then choose the brave and bold, cut off their returning army, set ambushes and strike with surprise, and attack head and tail; if they are not captured, they will still suffer a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 詔問：「輔翊之能，方面之才，與夫帥領偏裨，當今孰可以任此者？」

translations.literal: The edict asks, "Who among those fit to assist and support, regional talents, commanders, and deputy commanders of today can be entrusted with this?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict asks, "Who among those fit to assist and support, regional talents, commanders, and deputy commanders of today can be entrusted with this?"

sentences.zh: 臣以為不患無人，患有人而不能用爾。

translations.literal: I believe the trouble is not that there are no men, but that there are men who cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the trouble is not that there are no men, but that there are men who cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 今輔翊之臣，抱忠義之深者，莫如富弼。

translations.literal: Among assisting ministers today, none holds loyalty and righteousness so deep as Fu Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Among assisting ministers today, none holds loyalty and righteousness so deep as Fu Bi.

sentences.zh: 為社稷之固者，莫知范仲淹。

translations.literal: For securing the altars of state, none compares with Fan Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: For securing the altars of state, none compares with Fan Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 諳古今故事者，莫如夏竦。

translations.literal: For knowing ancient and modern precedents, none like Xia Song.
translations.idiomatic: For knowing ancient and modern precedents, none like Xia Song.

sentences.zh: 議論之敏者，莫如鄭戩。

translations.literal: For quickness in debate, none like Zheng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: For quickness in debate, none like Zheng Yan.

sentences.zh: 方面之才，嚴重有紀律者，莫如韓琦。

translations.literal: For regional talent, grave and disciplined, none like Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: For regional talent, grave and disciplined, none like Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 臨大事能斷者，莫如田況。

translations.literal: For facing great affairs and being able to decide, none like Tian Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: For facing great affairs and being able to decide, none like Tian Kuang.

sentences.zh: 剛果無顧避者，莫如劉渙。

translations.literal: For being resolute and bold without avoidance, none like Liu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: For being resolute and bold without avoidance, none like Liu Huan.

sentences.zh: 宏達有方略者，莫如孫沔。

translations.literal: For being broad-minded and having strategy, none like Sun Mian.
translations.idiomatic: For being broad-minded and having strategy, none like Sun Mian.

sentences.zh: 至於帥領偏裨，貴能坐運籌策，不必親當矢石，王德用素有威名，范仲淹深練軍政，龐籍久經邊任，皆其選也。

translations.literal: As for commanders and deputies, what is valued is the ability to sit and work out strategy and not necessarily face arrows in person; Wang Deyong has long had a fierce reputation, Fan Zhongyan is deeply versed in military affairs, and Pang Ji has long served on the border—all are fit choices.
translations.idiomatic: As for commanders and deputies, what is valued is the ability to sit and work out strategy and not necessarily face arrows in person; Wang Deyong has long had a fierce reputation, Fan Zhongyan is deeply versed in military affairs, and Pang Ji has long served on the border—all are fit choices.

sentences.zh: 狄青、范全頗能馭眾，蔣偕沉毅有術略，張亢倜儻有膽勇，劉貽孫材武剛斷，王德基純愨勁勇，此可補偏裨者也。

translations.literal: Di Qing and Fan Quan are quite able to command troops; Jiang Xie is steady and has strategy; Zhang Kang is bold and daring; Liu Yisun is martial and resolute; Wang Deji is pure, sincere, and fiercely brave—these can fill deputy posts.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing and Fan Quan are quite able to command troops; Jiang Xie is steady and has strategy; Zhang Kang is bold and daring; Liu Yisun is martial and resolute; Wang Deji is pure, sincere, and fiercely brave—these can fill deputy posts.

sentences.zh: 詔謂：「朔方災傷，軍儲缺乏。」

translations.literal: The edict states, "Shuofang has suffered disaster and military stores are lacking."
translations.idiomatic: The edict states, "Shuofang has suffered disaster and military stores are lacking."

sentences.zh: 此則三司失計置，轉運使不舉職，固非一日。

translations.literal: This is failure of planning by the Finance Commission and transport commissioners not performing their duties—it is not a matter of a single day.
translations.idiomatic: This is failure of planning by the Finance Commission and transport commissioners not performing their duties—it is not a matter of a single day.

sentences.zh: 既往固已不咎，來者又復不追，臣未見其可也。

translations.literal: The past is already not blamed, yet the future is again not pursued—I do not see how this can work.
translations.idiomatic: The past is already not blamed, yet the future is again not pursued—I do not see how this can work.

sentences.zh: 且如施昌言承久弊之政，方欲竭思慮、辦職事，一與賈昌朝違戾，遂被移徙，軍儲何由不乏？

translations.literal: Take Shi Changyan: he bore a long-corrupt policy and was just about to exhaust his thought and perform his duties, but once he clashed with Jia Changchao he was transferred—how then are military stores not to run short?
translations.idiomatic: Take Shi Changyan: he bore a long-corrupt policy and was just about to exhaust his thought and perform his duties, but once he clashed with Jia Changchao he was transferred—how then are military stores not to run short?

sentences.zh: 自去年秋八月，計度市糴，而昌朝執異議，仲春尚未與奪，財賦何緣得豐？

translations.literal: Since the eighth month of last autumn grain purchases were planned, yet Changchao held to a dissenting view and as late as mid-spring the matter was still undecided—how could revenues become abundant?
translations.idiomatic: Since the eighth month of last autumn grain purchases were planned, yet Changchao held to a dissenting view and as late as mid-spring the matter was still undecided—how could revenues become abundant?

sentences.zh: 先朝置內帑，本備非常。

translations.literal: The former court established the inner treasury to meet emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: The former court established the inner treasury to meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 今為主者之吝，自分彼我，緩急不以為備，則臣不知其所為也。

translations.literal: Now those in charge are stingy, divide what is theirs from what is ours, and do not use it when urgent or slow—I do not know what they are doing.
translations.idiomatic: Now those in charge are stingy, divide what is theirs from what is ours, and do not use it when urgent or slow—I do not know what they are doing.

sentences.zh: 至如粒食之重，轉徙為難，莫若重立爵等，少均萬數，豪民詿誤，使得入粟，以免杖笞，必能速辦。

translations.literal: As for the weight of grain and the difficulty of transport, nothing is better than restoring rank grades, slightly reducing the ten-thousand quotas, and letting wealthy men who have been misled be allowed to submit grain to avoid flogging—they will surely manage it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: As for the weight of grain and the difficulty of transport, nothing is better than restoring rank grades, slightly reducing the ten-thousand quotas, and letting wealthy men who have been misled be allowed to submit grain to avoid flogging—they will surely manage it quickly.

sentences.zh: 夫能儉嗇以省費，漸致於從容。

translations.literal: If one can be frugal and sparing to save expense, one may gradually reach ease.
translations.idiomatic: If one can be frugal and sparing to save expense, one may gradually reach ease.

sentences.zh: 德音及此，天下之福也。

translations.literal: If a virtuous edict reaches this point, it will be the realm's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If a virtuous edict reaches this point, it will be the realm's fortune.

sentences.zh: 比日多以卑官躐請厚奉，或身為內供奉而有遙刺之給，或為觀察使便占留後之封，幸門日開，賜予無藝，若令有司執守，率循舊規，庶幾物力亦獲寬弛。

translations.literal: Recently low officials have often leapt to request thick salaries, or served as inner attendants yet received stipends for remote prefectures, or served as observation commissioners yet kept acting military commissioner titles; the door of favor opens daily and gifts are boundless—if the responsible offices enforced the rules and followed the old regulations, perhaps material resources would also be eased.
translations.idiomatic: Recently low officials have often leapt to request thick salaries, or served as inner attendants yet received stipends for remote prefectures, or served as observation commissioners yet kept acting military commissioner titles; the door of favor opens daily and gifts are boundless—if the responsible offices enforced the rules and followed the old regulations, perhaps material resources would also be eased.

sentences.zh: 詔問：「戰馬乏絕，何策可使足用？」

translations.literal: The edict asks, "War horses are exhausted—what policy can make them sufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict asks, "War horses are exhausted—what policy can make them sufficient?"

sentences.zh: 臣前在三司，嘗陳監牧之弊，占良田九萬餘頃，歲費錢百萬緡。

translations.literal: When I was previously at the Finance Commission I once stated the abuses of the border pastures: they occupied more than ninety thousand qing of good land and spent a million strings a year.
translations.idiomatic: When I was previously at the Finance Commission I once stated the abuses of the border pastures: they occupied more than ninety thousand qing of good land and spent a million strings a year.

sentences.zh: 天閑之數，才三四萬，急有征調，一不可用。

translations.literal: The number in the imperial stables was only thirty or forty thousand, and when there was an urgent levy not one was usable.
translations.idiomatic: The number in the imperial stables was only thirty or forty thousand, and when there was an urgent levy not one was usable.

sentences.zh: 今欲不費而馬立辦，莫若賦馬於河北、河東、陝西、京東西五路。

translations.literal: If we now wish to have horses ready without expense, nothing is better than levying horses on the five circuits of Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and the capital east and west.
translations.idiomatic: If we now wish to have horses ready without expense, nothing is better than levying horses on the five circuits of Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and the capital east and west.

sentences.zh: 上戶一馬，中戶二戶一馬，養馬者復其一丁。

translations.literal: One horse for an upper household, one horse for every two middle households, and for those who raise horses one corvée laborer is remitted.
translations.idiomatic: One horse for an upper household, one horse for every two middle households, and for those who raise horses one corvée laborer is remitted.

sentences.zh: 如此，則坐致戰馬二十萬匹，不為難矣。」

translations.literal: In this way two hundred thousand war horses can be obtained seated—not difficult at all."
translations.idiomatic: In this way two hundred thousand war horses can be obtained seated—not difficult at all."

sentences.zh: 時清臣以河北乏兵食，自汴漕米繇河陰輸北道者七十餘萬；

translations.literal: At the time Qingchen, because Hebei lacked grain for the troops, transported more than seven hundred thousand from Bian grain transport via Heyin on the northern route;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qingchen, because Hebei lacked grain for the troops, transported more than seven hundred thousand from Bian grain transport via Heyin on the northern route;

sentences.zh: 又請發大名庫錢，以佐邊糴。

translations.literal: he also asked to release cash from the Daming treasury to aid border grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to release cash from the Daming treasury to aid border grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 而安撫使賈昌朝格詔不從，清臣固爭，且疏其跋扈不臣。

translations.literal: But Pacification Commissioner Jia Changchao blocked the edict and would not obey; Qingchen disputed firmly and also memorialized his arrogance and disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: But Pacification Commissioner Jia Changchao blocked the edict and would not obey; Qingchen disputed firmly and also memorialized his arrogance and disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 宰相方欲兩中之，乃徙昌朝鄭州，罷清臣為侍讀學士、知河陽。

translations.literal: The chancellors wished to split the difference, so Changchao was transferred to Zheng and Qingchen was dismissed to Reader and prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors wished to split the difference, so Changchao was transferred to Zheng and Qingchen was dismissed to Reader and prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously given Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 清臣天資爽邁，遇事敢行，奏對無所屈。

translations.literal: Qingchen was by nature clear and bold, acted boldly in affairs, and never bent in memorial replies.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was by nature clear and bold, acted boldly in affairs, and never bent in memorial replies.

sentences.zh: 郭承祐妻舒王元偁女，封郡主，給奉；

translations.literal: Guo Chengyou's wife was the daughter of the Prince of Shu, Wang Yuanzheng; she was enfeoffed as county princess and given a salary;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengyou's wife was the daughter of the Prince of Shu, Wang Yuanzheng; she was enfeoffed as county princess and given a salary;

sentences.zh: 及承祐為殿前副都指揮使，妻以不加封，請增月給，清臣執奏不可。

translations.literal: when Chengyou became Deputy Commander of the Palace Front, his wife, though not given an added title, asked for an increased monthly stipend; Qingchen insisted in memorial that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: when Chengyou became Deputy Commander of the Palace Front, his wife, though not given an added title, asked for an increased monthly stipend; Qingchen insisted in memorial that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「承祐管軍，妻又諸王女，當優之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said, "Chengyou commands the army and his wife is also a prince's daughter; she should be favored."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "Chengyou commands the army and his wife is also a prince's daughter; she should be favored."

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「是終為僥幸。」

translations.literal: Qingchen said, "That would end as favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said, "That would end as favoritism."

sentences.zh: 遂卷其奏置懷中，不行。

translations.literal: He then rolled up his memorial, placed it in his bosom, and did not enact it.
translations.idiomatic: He then rolled up his memorial, placed it in his bosom, and did not enact it.

sentences.zh: 數上書論天下事，陳九議、十要、五利，皆當世可行者。

translations.literal: He often memorialized on affairs of the realm, setting forth Nine Discussions, Ten Essentials, and Five Benefits, all feasible in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He often memorialized on affairs of the realm, setting forth Nine Discussions, Ten Essentials, and Five Benefits, all feasible in his age.

sentences.zh: 有文集一百六十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in one hundred and sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in one hundred and sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 子均，為集賢校理。

translations.literal: His son Jun served as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun served as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 楊察，字隱甫。

translations.literal: Yang Cha, style name Yinfu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cha, whose courtesy name was Yinfu,

sentences.zh: 其先晉人，從唐僖宗入蜀，家於成都。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Jin; following Emperor Xizong of Tang into Shu, they settled in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: came from Jin stock; his forebears followed Emperor Xizong of Tang into Shu and made their home in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 至其祖鈞，始從孟昶歸朝。

translations.literal: By the time of his grandfather Jun they first followed Meng Chang in submitting to the Song court.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun was the first to leave Meng Chang and submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 鈞生居簡，仕真宗時，至尚書都官員外郎，嘗官廬州，遂為合肥人。

translations.literal: Jun begot Ju Jian, who served under Emperor Zhenzong and reached Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; having once served in Luzhou, he became a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Ju Jian served under Emperor Zhenzong, rising to vice director in the Ministry of Justice; after an appointment in Luzhou, the family became natives of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 居簡生察，景祐元年，舉進士甲科，除將作監丞、通判宿州。

translations.literal: Ju Jian begot Cha; in the first year of Jingyou he passed the jinshi examination in the top class and was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Jian's son Cha placed in the top class of the jinshi in the first year of Jingyou and was made vice director of the directorate of palace buildings and vice prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書省著作郎、直集賢院，出知潁、壽二州，入為開封府推官，判三司鹽鐵、度支勾院，修起居注，歷江南東路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to drafting secretary in the Secretariat, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, went out to govern Ying and Shou prefectures, entered as investigating judge of the Kaifeng prefecture, judged the Salt and Iron and Revenue Commissions, revised the Veritable Records, and served as transport commissioner on the Jiangnan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to drafting secretary in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, governed Ying and Shou, returned as investigating judge in Kaifeng, judged the salt and revenue offices, revised the Veritable Records, and served as transport commissioner on the Jiangnan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬吏以察年少，易之。

translations.literal: His subordinates, because Cha was young, treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His staff, seeing how young he was, took him lightly.

sentences.zh: 及行部，數摘姦隱，眾始畏伏。

translations.literal: When he made his inspection tour he repeatedly exposed hidden wrongdoing, and all began to fear and submit.
translations.idiomatic: On his inspection rounds he repeatedly uncovered hidden abuses, and everyone soon learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 察在部，專以舉官為急務。

translations.literal: While in his circuit Cha made recommending officials his urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: In his circuit Cha made recommending officials his chief priority.

sentences.zh: 人或議之，察曰：「此按察職也，苟掎拾羨餘，則俗吏之能，何必我哉！」

translations.literal: When some criticized this, Cha said: "This is the duty of an inspector; if I merely picked at surplus profit, any petty clerk could do it — why need me?"
translations.idiomatic: When some objected, Cha said: "That is an inspector's proper work; if I merely picked at petty surpluses, any clerk could do it — why need me?"

sentences.zh: 召為右正言、知制誥，權判禮部貢院。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Remonstrator and drafter of edicts, and concurrently supervised the Ministry of Rites examination hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right remonstrator and drafter of edicts, and concurrently supervised the Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 時上封者請罷有司糊名考士，及變文格，使為放軼以襲唐體。

translations.literal: At the time memorialists asked to abolish the ministry's practice of sealing names in examining candidates, and to change the literary format, making compositions loose to imitate Tang style.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists then asked to end the sealing of candidates' names in examinations and to change the literary format, urging loose compositions in imitation of Tang style.

sentences.zh: 察以謂：「防禁一潰，則奔競復起。

translations.literal: Cha held that "once the barriers are breached, competition will rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Cha argued that "once the barriers are breached, competition will rise again.

sentences.zh: 且文無今昔，惟以體要為宗，若肆其澶漫，亦非唐氏科選之法。」

translations.literal: Moreover, literature has no ancient and modern — only substance and essentials matter as the standard; if one indulges in sprawling excess, that too is not the Tang method of selecting by examination."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, good writing knows no ancient or modern divide — only substance counts; indulgent sprawling prose is not the Tang way of selecting talent by examination either."

sentences.zh: 前議遂寢。

translations.literal: The earlier proposal thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 晏殊執政，以妻父嫌，換龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: When Yan Shu held power, because of his wife's father he was transferred to awaiting appointment in the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shu was in power, a conflict involving his wife's father led to his transfer to awaiting appointment in the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，服除，復為知制誥，拜翰林學士、權知開封府，擢右諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother; when the mourning ended he again became drafter of edicts, was made Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng, and was promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor and acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; when mourning ended he again drafted edicts, became Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Kaifeng, and was promoted to right remonstrating censor and acting vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 論事無所避。

translations.literal: In discussing affairs he shrank from nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he shrank from nothing.

sentences.zh: 會詔舉御史，建言：「臺屬供奉殿中，巡糾不法，必得通古今治亂良直之臣。

translations.literal: When an edict called for recommending censors, he submitted: "Censorate staff attend in the palace hall and patrol to correct violations of law; they must be men who thoroughly know the rise and fall of ages and are upright — truly so.
translations.idiomatic: When the court called for censor nominations, he wrote: "Censors attend in the hall and patrol to correct violations; they must be men who know the rise and fall of ages and are upright in character.

sentences.zh: 今舉格太密，公坐細故，皆置不取，恐英偉之士，或有所遺。」

translations.literal: Today the criteria for recommendation are too tight; for public faults and minor matters all are set aside and not taken — I fear outstanding men may be overlooked."
translations.idiomatic: Today the criteria are too tight; minor public faults disqualify candidates, and I fear outstanding men are being overlooked."

sentences.zh: 御史何郯以論事不得實，中書問狀。

translations.literal: Censor He Yan was questioned by the Secretariat because his discussion of affairs lacked substantiation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Yan was questioned by the Secretariat because his policy arguments lacked substantiation.

sentences.zh: 察又言：「御史，故事許風聞；

translations.literal: Cha also said: "Censors, by precedent, are allowed to act on rumor;
translations.idiomatic: Cha also said: "Censors, by precedent, may act on rumor;

sentences.zh: 縱所言不當，自係朝廷采擇。

translations.literal: even if what they say is not correct, that still lies with the court to choose.
translations.idiomatic: even if their reports prove wrong, the court still decides what to accept.

sentences.zh: 今以疑似之間，遽被詰問，臣恐臺諫官畏罪緘默，非所以廣言路也。」

translations.literal: Now on the basis of mere suspicion they are suddenly interrogated — I fear censors and remonstrators will fear punishment and fall silent, which is not how to broaden the path of speech."
translations.idiomatic: Now on mere suspicion they are interrogated — I fear remonstrators will fall silent for fear of punishment, and that is not how to keep the path of speech open."

sentences.zh: 又數以言事忤宰相陳執中。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly spoke on affairs in opposition to Chief Councilor Chen Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He also clashed repeatedly with Chief Councilor Chen Zhizhong over policy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三司戶部判官楊儀以請求貶官，察坐前在府失出笞罪，雖去官，猶罷知信州。

translations.literal: Before long, Revenue Commission judge Yang Yi was demoted for seeking favors; Cha was punished because while previously in the prefecture he had failed to report a beating offense — though he had left that office, he was still stripped of his post as prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Revenue judge Yang Yi was demoted for seeking favors; Cha was punished for failing, while prefect earlier, to report a beating offense — though he had left that post, he was still removed as prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙揚州，復為翰林侍讀學士，又兼龍圖閣學士、知永興軍，加端明殿學士、知益州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Yangzhou, again made Hanlin attendant academician, also given the Dragon Diagram academician title and made prefect of Yongxing Army, then added as academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Yangzhou, again made Hanlin attendant academician, also made Dragon Diagram academician and prefect of Yongxing, then academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎，復權知開封府，復兼翰林學士、權三司使。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, again acted as prefect of Kaifeng, and again concurrently served as Hanlin academician and acting commissioner of the Revenue Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Twice promoted to vice minister of rites, he again acted as Kaifeng prefect and again served concurrently as Hanlin academician and acting revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 內侍楊永德毀察於帝，三司有獄，辭連衛士，皇城司不即遣，而有詔移開封府鞫之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Yang Yongde slandered Cha to the emperor; the Revenue Commission had a case in which testimony implicated guards, and the Imperial City Bureau did not promptly send them — yet there was an edict transferring the case to Kaifeng for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendant Yang Yongde slandered Cha to the emperor; a revenue case implicated palace guards, and the Imperial City Bureau delayed sending them — yet an edict moved the trial to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 察由是乞罷三司，乃遷戶部侍郎兼三學士，提連集禧觀，進承旨。

translations.literal: Cha therefore asked to leave the Revenue Commission and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue with the three academician titles, put in charge of Jixi Abbey, and advanced to chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: Cha asked to leave the Revenue Commission and was made vice minister of revenue with three academician titles, put in charge of Jixi Abbey, and promoted to chief academician.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復以本官充三司使。

translations.literal: After a year he again filled his former post as revenue commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he again served as revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 餌鍾乳過劑，病癰卒。

translations.literal: He took too large a dose of stalactite medicine and died of a carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: He took an overdose of stalactite elixir and died of a carbuncle.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡宣懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with posthumous title Xuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of rites, with the posthumous title Xuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 察美風儀。

translations.literal: Cha had a fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，七歲始能言，母頗知書，嘗自教之。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he could speak only at seven; his mother knew books well and often taught him herself.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he did not speak until seven; his mother was literate and taught him herself.

sentences.zh: 敏於屬文，其為制誥，初若不用意；

translations.literal: Quick at literary composition; in drafting edicts he at first seemed not to labor;
translations.idiomatic: Quick with the brush, he seemed at first not to labor over edicts;

sentences.zh: 及稿成，皆雅致有體，當世稱之。

translations.literal: when the draft was finished, all were elegant and well-formed, and his age praised them.
translations.idiomatic: yet the finished drafts were always elegant and well-formed, and his contemporaries praised them.

sentences.zh: 遇事明決，勤於吏職，雖多益喜不厭。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was clear and decisive, diligent in official duty, and though tasks multiplied he was never weary.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and decisive in affairs, diligent in office, he never wearied though duties multiplied.

sentences.zh: 癰方作，猶入對，商畫財利，歸而大頓，人以為用神太竭云。

translations.literal: When the carbuncle first formed he still entered audience and discussed finance; returning home he collapsed severely — people said he had exhausted his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When the abscess first formed he still attended audience to discuss finance; returning home he collapsed — people said he had exhausted his spirit.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子庶為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took his elder brother's son Shu as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his elder brother's son Shu as heir.

sentences.zh: 弟寘，舉進士第一，通判潤州，以母憂不赴，毀瘠而卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhi placed first in the jinshi examination, was made vice prefect of Runzhou, but did not take up the post on mourning for his mother and died wasted away by grief.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhi placed first in the jinshi, was appointed vice prefect of Runzhou, but did not take up the post while mourning his mother and died wasted away by grief.

sentences.zh: 時人傷之。

translations.literal: People of the time mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當仁宗在位時，宋興且百年，海內嘉靖，上下安佚。

translations.literal: The commentators say: During Renzong's reign the Song had risen for nearly a hundred years; within the seas all was tranquil, above and below at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Under Renzong the Song dynasty had stood for nearly a century; within the seas all was tranquil, and court and country were at ease.

sentences.zh: 然法制日以玩弛，僥幸之弊多。

translations.literal: Yet institutions daily grew lax, and the abuses of opportunism multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet institutions grew lax by the day, and opportunism spread.

sentences.zh: 自西陲用兵，關中困擾，天子憫勞元元，奮然欲用群材以更內外之治，於時俊傑輩出。

translations.literal: Once war began on the western frontier and Guanzhong was troubled, the Son of Heaven pitied the people and roused himself to employ talented men to renew governance within and without; at that time outstanding men emerged in throngs.
translations.idiomatic: When war opened on the western frontier and Guanzhong was harried, the emperor pitied the people and roused himself to employ talent to renew governance at home and abroad — and outstanding men emerged in throngs.

sentences.zh: 尹洙崎嶇兵間，亦頗論天下之事。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu, struggling through military campaigns, also discussed affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu, struggling through the campaigns, also spoke broadly on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 孫甫馳騁言路，咸以文學、方正知名。

translations.literal: Sun Fu charged along the path of remonstrance; both were renowned for learning and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu charged along the path of remonstrance; both were famed for learning and upright character.

sentences.zh: 絳文詞議論，尤為儒林所宗。

translations.literal: Jiang's literary compositions and policy discussions were especially honored in the Confucian community.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's writings and policy debates were especially honored among Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方欲倚用之，不幸死矣。

translations.literal: The court was just then about to rely on him when he unfortunately died.
translations.idiomatic: The court was just then preparing to rely on him when he died untimely.

sentences.zh: 最後，清臣、察繇進士高等，不數年致位侍從，立朝謇謇，無所附麗，為一時名臣。

translations.literal: Last came Qingchen and Cha, who from top jinshi ranks within a few years reached attendance on the throne; upright in court, attached to no faction, they were famed ministers of their age.
translations.idiomatic: Last came Qingchen and Cha, who from top jinshi ranks reached attendance within a few years; upright in court and tied to no faction, they were famed ministers of their day.

sentences.zh: 豈非出於上之所自擢，故奮勵不撓，以圖報稱哉？

translations.literal: Was this not because they were raised up by the sovereign himself, and therefore strove without bending to repay his favor?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because the sovereign himself had raised them up, so that they strove without bending to repay his trust?
